occasions.name: Islamic New Year
occasions.note: The first day of Muharram, a sacred month. The calendar counts from the Hijrah.

occasions.name: Day of Ashura
occasions.note: Fasting Ashura expiates the sins of the previous year, and it is recommended to fast the 9th or 11th with it (Muslim). The Prophet ﷺ found the Jews of Madinah fasting it because Allah saved Musa on that day (Bukhari).

occasions.name: The Prophet’s arrival in Madinah and his passing (traditional date)
occasions.note: The classical historians give 12 Rabi‘ al-Awwal for his arrival in Madinah in 1 AH, and for his passing in 11 AH. His birth is also commonly given on this date, though scholars differ about the day.

occasions.name: Battle of Hattin (583 AH)
occasions.note: On 24 Rabi‘ ath-Thani 583 AH (4 July 1187 CE), Salah ad-Din defeated the Crusader army and opened the way to Jerusalem.

occasions.name: Fall of Constantinople (857 AH)
occasions.note: On 20 Jumada al-Ula 857 AH (29 May 1453 CE) the city fell to Sultan Muhammad al-Fatih, as the Prophet ﷺ had foretold to his community.

occasions.name: Passing of Abu Bakr (13 AH)
occasions.note: The first caliph died on 22 Jumada ath-Thaniyah, two years and about three months after the Prophet ﷺ.

occasions.name: Rajab begins
occasions.note: One of the four sacred months in which Allah forbade fighting and wrongdoing (Qur’an 9:36).

occasions.name: The Night Journey, as remembered by many Muslims
occasions.note: Many Muslims remember the Isra’ and Mi‘raj on 27 Rajab. Scholars say that the exact night is not established by an authentic report. Salah ad-Din entered Jerusalem on this date in 583 AH.

occasions.name: Sha‘ban begins
occasions.note: ‘A’ishah said that the Prophet ﷺ fasted more in Sha‘ban than in any other month (Bukhari and Muslim).

occasions.name: Ramadan begins
occasions.note: The month of fasting, the Qur’an and mercy.

occasions.name: Birth of al-Hasan (3 AH)
occasions.note: The Prophet’s first grandson by Fatimah and ‘Ali, born in the middle of Ramadan in the third year, according to most historians.

occasions.name: Battle of Badr (2 AH)
occasions.note: On 17 Ramadan, the Muslims, about three hundred strong, met Quraysh at Badr, and Allah gave them victory on the day He called the Day of Criterion (Qur’an 8:41).

occasions.name: The conquest of Makkah (8 AH)
occasions.note: The Prophet ﷺ entered Makkah in Ramadan of the eighth year, most commonly dated to the 20th, and forgave its people.

occasions.name: Last ten nights of Ramadan
occasions.note: Seek Laylat al-Qadr in the odd nights of the last ten (Bukhari).

occasions.name: Passing of ‘Ali (40 AH)
occasions.note: The fourth caliph was struck while praying in the mosque of Kufa and died of the wound on 21 Ramadan.

occasions.name: ‘Ayn Jalut (658 AH)
occasions.note: On 25 Ramadan 658 AH (3 September 1260 CE), the Mamluk army under Qutuz and Baybars defeated a Mongol army in Palestine.

occasions.name: The 27th night of Ramadan
occasions.note: Ubayy ibn Ka‘b used to swear that Laylat al-Qadr was the 27th night (Muslim). Its exact night is hidden: seek it in the odd nights of the last ten.

occasions.name: Eid al-Fitr
occasions.note: Fasting on this day is not permitted (Bukhari and Muslim).

occasions.name: Six days of Shawwal
occasions.note: Whoever fasts Ramadan then follows it with six days of Shawwal, it is as if he fasted the whole year (Muslim).

occasions.name: Battle of Uhud (3 AH)
occasions.note: On Saturday 7 Shawwal, the Muslims met Quraysh at the foot of Mount Uhud. Hamzah was killed, and the Prophet ﷺ was wounded.

occasions.name: Dhul-Qa‘dah begins
occasions.note: A sacred month. In it the Prophet ﷺ made three of his four ‘Umrahs, including Hudaybiyyah in 6 AH.

occasions.name: First ten days of Dhul Hijjah
occasions.note: No deeds are more beloved to Allah than righteous deeds in these days (Bukhari).

occasions.name: Day of Tarwiyah
occasions.note: The pilgrims go to Mina and spend the day and night there.

occasions.name: Day of Arafah
occasions.note: Fasting Arafah, for those not on Hajj, expiates the previous and the coming year (Muslim).

occasions.name: The Farewell Sermon (10 AH)
occasions.note: On the Day of Arafah in the tenth year, the Prophet ﷺ spoke to more than a hundred thousand Muslims in the valley of ‘Uranah.

occasions.name: Eid al-Adha
occasions.note: The Day of Sacrifice.

occasions.name: Days of Tashriq
occasions.note: The 11th, 12th and 13th are days of eating, drinking and remembering Allah (Muslim). Fasting on them is not allowed except for those who could not offer the hady.

occasions.name: Martyrdom of ‘Uthman (35 AH)
occasions.note: The third caliph was killed in his house in Madinah in Dhul-Hijjah of 35 AH, while reciting the Qur’an, according to the classical historians.

occasions.name: ‘Umar is struck (23 AH)
occasions.note: The second caliph was stabbed while leading the dawn prayer, and died three days later. He was buried at the beginning of Muharram.

collections.title: Duas from the Qur’an
collections.blurb: Supplications of the prophets and the righteous, in the words Allah recorded.

collections.title: Protection & refuge
collections.blurb: The verses and surahs the Prophet ﷺ taught for seeking Allah’s protection.

facts.t: Whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi when going to bed, a guardian from Allah stays with him and Satan will not come near him until morning.
Whoever recites the last two verses of Surah al-Baqarah at night, they will be enough for him.
Recite Surah al-Ikhlas and the two Mu’awwidhat (al-Falaq and an-Nas) three times in the morning and in the evening; they will be enough for you against everything.
Nothing stands between the one who recites Ayat al-Kursi after each obligatory prayer and entering Paradise except death.

collections.title: Friday (Jumu’ah)
collections.blurb: The best day of the week.

facts.t: Whoever recites Surah al-Kahf on Friday, a light will shine for him between the two Fridays.
Send abundant blessings upon me on Friday.
On Friday there is an hour in which a Muslim who asks Allah for good while standing in prayer will be given it.

collections.title: Ramadan & Laylat al-Qadr
collections.blurb: The month of fasting, and the night better than a thousand months.

facts.t: Whoever fasts Ramadan with faith and seeking reward, his previous sins will be forgiven.
Whoever stands in prayer on Laylat al-Qadr with faith and seeking reward, his previous sins will be forgiven.
Seek Laylat al-Qadr in the odd nights of the last ten nights of Ramadan.
Whoever gives a fasting person something to break his fast with earns the same reward as him, without lessening the fasting person’s reward.

dua.ar: اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّكَ عَفُوٌّ تُحِبُّ الْعَفْوَ فَاعْفُ عَنِّي
dua.en: O Allah, You are Pardoning and You love to pardon, so pardon me.
dua.src: The supplication the Prophet ﷺ taught ‘A’ishah for Laylat al-Qadr: at-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah
dua.title: Dua for Laylat al-Qadr

collections.title: Eid
collections.blurb: Takbeer, gratitude and sacrifice.

dua.ar: اللهُ أَكْبَرُ اللهُ أَكْبَرُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ، وَاللهُ أَكْبَرُ اللهُ أَكْبَرُ وَلِلَّهِ الْحَمْدُ
dua.en: Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest. There is no god but Allah. Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, and to Allah belongs all praise.
dua.tl: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar, la ilaha illallah, wallahu akbar, Allahu akbar, wa lillahil-hamd.
dua.src: The customary Takbeer of Eid, reported from the Companions (Ibn Abi Shaybah)
dua.title: Takbeer of Eid

dua.en: May Allah accept it from us and from you.
dua.src: The greeting the Companions exchanged on Eid
dua.title: Eid greeting

collections.title: Hajj & the Sacred House
collections.blurb: Verses about the Ka’bah and the pilgrimage, with the supplications of the rites.

collections.title: Patience & hardship
collections.blurb: Verses for difficult times.

facts.t: How wonderful is the affair of the believer: all of it is good for him. If something good happens to him he is grateful, and that is good for him; if something harmful happens to him he is patient, and that is good for him.

collections.title: Gratitude & praise
collections.blurb: Thanking Allah for what we have.

collections.title: Forgiveness & mercy
collections.blurb: Returning to Allah.

facts.t: Every son of Adam sins, and the best of those who sin are those who repent.

collections.title: Knowledge & guidance
collections.blurb: Asking Allah for understanding and the straight path.

facts.t: Whoever treads a path seeking knowledge, Allah makes easy for him a path to Paradise.

collections.title: Parents & family
collections.blurb: Kindness to parents and prayers for children and spouses.

facts.t: The pleasure of the Lord is in the pleasure of the parent, and the anger of the Lord is in the anger of the parent.

collections.title: Trust in Allah (tawakkul)
collections.blurb: Verses on relying on Allah after doing your part.

facts.t: If you relied on Allah as He should be relied upon, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds: they go out hungry in the morning and return full.
facts.s: Sunan at-Tirmidhi, hasan; Sunan Ibn Majah

collections.title: The night prayer
collections.blurb: The believers who rise in the night, in the words of the Qur’an.

facts.t: The best prayer after the obligatory prayers is the prayer in the night.

Our Lord descends to the lowest heaven in the last third of the night and says: Who calls upon Me that I may answer him? Who asks Me that I may give him? Who seeks My forgiveness that I may forgive him?

collections.title: The mercy of Allah
collections.blurb: Verses of hope for the one who has fallen short.

facts.t: When Allah decreed the creation, He wrote in a book that is with Him above the Throne: My mercy prevails over My wrath.

collections.title: Reflecting on creation
collections.blurb: Verses that invite you to look at the sky, the earth and yourself.

facts.t: The Prophet ﷺ used to recite the last ten verses of Surah Al ‘Imran when he woke at night.

collections.title: Character and manners
collections.blurb: Verses on how a believer speaks, behaves and treats others.

facts.t: The most beloved of you to me, and the nearest to me on the Day of Resurrection, are those with the best character.
I was sent only to perfect the best of character.

collections.title: Justice
collections.blurb: Standing for fairness, even against yourself.

facts.t: The just will be on pulpits of light beside the Most Merciful, on His right: those who are just in their rulings, with their families and in what they are given charge of.

collections.title: Brotherhood and unity
collections.blurb: The bond between believers.

facts.t: The believers in their mutual love, mercy and compassion are like one body: when one part complains, the whole body responds with sleeplessness and fever.

collections.title: Giving and spending
collections.blurb: Verses on charity, generosity and the use of wealth.

facts.t: Charity does not decrease wealth.
Every day two angels descend: one says, O Allah, give the one who spends something in return; the other says, O Allah, give the one who withholds destruction.

collections.title: Hope and ease
collections.blurb: Verses to hold on to in a hard time.

facts.t: Know that victory comes with patience, relief with affliction, and ease with hardship.

collections.title: This life and the next
collections.blurb: Reminders that this world is a passing stop on the way.

facts.t: Be in this world as though you were a stranger or a traveller.
Remember often the destroyer of pleasures, which is death.

fasting.n: Deeds are presented to Allah on these days, and the Prophet ﷺ loved to be fasting when his deeds were presented.

fasting.t: The White Days (13th, 14th and 15th of each month)
fasting.n: The Prophet ﷺ advised fasting three days every month.
fasting.s: Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim; an-Nasa’i for the White Days

fasting.n: Whoever fasts Ramadan and follows it with six days of Shawwal, it is as if he fasted the whole year.

fasting.t: The Day of Arafah (9 Dhul Hijjah)
fasting.n: It expiates the sins of the previous year and the coming year, for those who are not on Hajj.
It expiates the sins of the previous year. It is recommended to fast the 9th or the 11th with it.
The best fasting after Ramadan is in Allah’s month of Muharram.

fasting.t: Days on which fasting is not permitted

nawawi.s: Deeds are only as good as the intention behind them, and each person gets what they intended. Emigrating for Allah and His Messenger is rewarded as such; emigrating for worldly gain or marriage counts only for that.

Jibril, appearing as a stranger, asks the Prophet ﷺ about Islam, faith (iman), excellence (ihsan), the Hour and its signs. Islam is the five pillars; iman is the six articles of belief; ihsan is to worship Allah as though you see Him, for even if you do not see Him, He sees you.
Islam is built on five: the testimony of faith, establishing prayer, giving zakat, pilgrimage to the House, and fasting Ramadan.

A human being is formed in the womb in stages, then an angel is sent to breathe in the soul and to record four things: provision, lifespan, deeds, and whether they will be wretched or blessed. Deeds are judged by how they end.
Whoever introduces into this matter of ours something that is not part of it will have it rejected.

nawawi.t: The lawful and the unlawful are clear
nawawi.s: What is lawful is clear and what is unlawful is clear, and between them are doubtful matters. Whoever avoids doubtful matters protects his religion and honour. In the body is a piece of flesh: if it is sound, the whole body is sound; it is the heart.
The religion is naseehah (sincerity and sincere advice): to Allah, to His Book, to His Messenger, to the leaders of the Muslims and to their common people.

nawawi.t: The sanctity of life and property
nawawi.s: Those who testify to the faith, establish prayer and give zakat have their lives and property protected, except by the right of Islam, and their reckoning is with Allah.

nawawi.t: Do what you are able to
nawawi.s: Avoid what the Prophet ﷺ forbade; do what he commanded as much as you can. Earlier nations were destroyed by their excessive questioning and their disputes with their prophets.

nawawi.t: Allah accepts only what is pure
nawawi.s: Allah is pure and accepts only what is pure. He commanded the believers as He commanded the messengers: eat of the good things and do righteous deeds. A traveller who raises his hands in dua while his food, drink and clothing are unlawful, how can he be answered?
Leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt.

nawawi.t: Leave what does not concern you
nawawi.s: Part of the excellence of a person’s Islam is leaving what does not concern him.

nawawi.t: Love for your brother what you love for yourself
nawawi.s: None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.

nawawi.t: The sanctity of a Muslim’s blood
nawawi.s: A Muslim’s blood may not be shed except in three cases: a married person who commits adultery, a life for a life, and one who abandons his religion and leaves the community. Such penalties belong only to the lawful authority and the courts.
Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or keep silent; should honour his neighbour; and should honour his guest.
A man asked for advice and the Prophet ﷺ told him, repeatedly: "Do not become angry."
Allah has prescribed excellence (ihsan) in everything. Even when slaughtering, do it well: sharpen the blade and spare the animal suffering.
Be mindful of Allah wherever you are; follow a bad deed with a good one and it will erase it; and treat people with good character.

nawawi.t: Allah will protect those who protect His rights
nawawi.s: Guard Allah and He will guard you. When you ask, ask Allah; when you seek help, seek help from Allah. Even if the whole nation gathered to benefit you, they could only do so by what Allah has written for you. The pens are lifted and the pages are dry.
Among what people inherited from the words of earlier prophets: "If you feel no shame, do as you wish." Modesty is a guard against doing wrong.
A man asked for a statement about Islam he need ask no one else about. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Say, I believe in Allah, then be steadfast."

A man asked whether he would enter Paradise if he prayed the obligatory prayers, fasted Ramadan, treated the lawful as lawful and the unlawful as unlawful, and did nothing more. The Prophet ﷺ said yes.

Purity is half of faith. "Alhamdulillah" fills the scale. Prayer is light, charity is proof, patience is illumination, and the Qur’an is a proof for you or against you. Every person starts the day either freeing himself or ruining himself.

Allah says: "O My servants, I have forbidden oppression for Myself and made it forbidden among you, so do not oppress one another." All guidance, food and clothing come from Him, so ask Him. Only deeds are recorded and returned; whoever finds good should praise Allah, and whoever finds otherwise should blame only himself.
The Companions said the wealthy take the rewards by giving charity. The Prophet ﷺ replied that every tasbih, takbir, tahmid and tahlil is charity, as are enjoining good and forbidding evil.
Every joint of a person owes charity each day: judging justly between two people, helping someone onto their mount, a good word, every step towards prayer, and removing harm from the road.
Righteousness is good character, and sin is what stirs in your heart and what you dislike people finding out about.
The Prophet ﷺ gave a moving sermon: fear Allah, listen and obey, and hold fast to his Sunnah and that of the rightly guided caliphs. Beware of newly invented matters in religion.
Mu’adh asked for a deed that enters him into Paradise. The Prophet ﷺ named the pillars of Islam, then the doors of goodness (fasting, charity, night prayer), and told him to guard his tongue.

nawawi.t: Respect the limits Allah has set
nawawi.s: Allah has set obligations, so do not neglect them; set limits, so do not transgress them; forbidden things, so do not violate them; and has been silent about some things out of mercy, so do not go searching for them.
A man asked for a deed that would make Allah and people love him. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Be detached from the world and Allah will love you; be detached from what people have and people will love you."

nawawi.t: No harm and no reciprocating harm
nawawi.s: There is to be no harming and no reciprocating harm: a foundation of Islamic ethics and law.
If people were given whatever they claimed, some would claim the wealth and blood of others. The burden of proof is on the claimant, and the oath is on the one who denies.
Whoever sees something wrong should change it with his hand; if he cannot, then with his tongue; if he cannot, then with his heart, and that is the weakest of faith.

Do not envy, deceive, hate or turn away from one another. A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim: he does not wrong him, abandon him, lie to him or look down on him. Piety is here (the chest). The blood, wealth and honour of a Muslim are sacred.

Whoever relieves a believer of a worldly hardship, Allah relieves him of a hardship on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever eases the burden of a debtor, conceals a Muslim’s fault, or seeks knowledge, Allah will ease, conceal and ease the path to Paradise for him. Allah helps His servant while he helps his brother.

Whoever intends a good deed but does not do it, Allah records one full good deed; if he does it, ten up to seven hundred times or more. Whoever intends a bad deed and does not do it, Allah records a full good deed; if he does it, one bad deed.

Allah says: nothing brings My servant closer to Me than what I made obligatory for him, and My servant keeps drawing nearer to Me with voluntary deeds until I love him. When I love him, I am his hearing, sight, hand and foot; if he asks Me, I give him, and if he seeks refuge in Me, I protect him.
Allah has pardoned for my nation mistakes, forgetfulness and what they are forced to do.

nawawi.t: Be like a stranger in this world
nawawi.s: Be in this world as though you were a stranger or a traveller. Ibn Umar added: when evening comes do not wait for morning, and when morning comes do not wait for evening; take from your health for your illness and from your life for your death.

nawawi.t: Desires follow what the Prophet brought
nawawi.s: None of you truly believes until his desires follow what the Prophet ﷺ brought.
nawawi.src: Related by an-Nawawi in al-Hujjah with a sound chain

nawawi.t: The vastness of Allah’s forgiveness (Hadith Qudsi)
nawawi.s: Allah says: "O son of Adam, as long as you call on Me and hope in Me, I will forgive you whatever you have done. If your sins reached the clouds of the sky and you asked My forgiveness, I would forgive you. If you came to Me with an earth-full of sins but met Me not associating anything with Me, I would bring you an earth-full of forgiveness."

names: The One God, the Lord of all that exists
The Trustee, the Disposer of affairs
The Counter, who accounts for everything
The Self-Subsisting, the Sustainer of all
The Lord of Majesty and Generosity
The Guide to the right path

shelves.title: Tales from the Qur’an
shelves.blurb: People, places and moments the Qur’an tells us about, each with a lesson for today.

shelves.title: The Life of the Prophet ﷺ
shelves.blurb: From the Year of the Elephant to his passing, step by step.

shelves.title: The Companions
shelves.blurb: Ordinary people changed by faith, and what they did with it.

shelves.title: Teachings in Real Moments
shelves.blurb: What the Prophet ﷺ said and did when something actually happened.

shelves.blurb: Accounts of earlier people that the Prophet ﷺ told his Companions, each with a lesson he drew or that the story carries.

shelves.title: Women of Faith
shelves.blurb: Women the Qur’an and the Sunnah hold up as examples: mothers, wives, scholars and fighters for what is right.

shelves.title: Scholars and Seekers
shelves.blurb: The scholars who preserved and explained the religion, and what they gave up to do it.

shelves.title: Moments in History
shelves.blurb: Turning points after the Prophet ﷺ: how the calendar began, a city surrendered with a promise, and people whose work reached far.

stories.title: Adam and the first test
p: Allah told the angels He was placing a successor on the earth. He created Adam from clay, taught him the names of things, and commanded the angels to prostrate to him. All did, except Iblis, who refused out of pride: "I am better than him."

Adam and his wife were placed in Paradise and told to eat freely, but not to approach one tree. Satan whispered to them, promising a life that never ends, and they ate. Realising what they had done, they did not blame each other or argue. They turned to Allah: "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers."
Allah accepted their repentance and sent them to the earth with guidance for all who would follow.
l: Pride was the first sin; humility is the way back.
Everyone slips. What matters is turning to Allah quickly instead of making excuses.
The earth was never a punishment: it is where guidance and purpose begin.

stories.title: Idris, the truthful
p: The Qur’an mentions Idris in two short verses. He was a truthful man and a prophet, and Allah raised him to a high station.
Though little is told, the description is enough: truthfulness and prophethood together are what the Qur’an remembers him for.
l: A person can be remembered for one quality done sincerely.
Truthfulness is the first mark of a prophet, and a standard for us.

stories.title: Nuh and the Ark
p: Nuh called his people to worship Allah alone, night and day, in public and in private, for 950 years. Only a few believed. The leaders mocked him: "We see no one following you except the lowest of us." He answered that he would never drive away the believers, whoever they were.

When Allah told him no more would believe, he began building an ark on dry land, and passing people laughed. Then the flood came. Nuh called to his son to board; the son said he would climb a mountain. The wave came between them and the son was among the drowned.
Nuh asked about his son, and Allah replied that he was not of his family in faith, for his deeds were not righteous. The ark came to rest on Mount Judi, and the earth was told to swallow its water.
l: Keep calling people with patience, even when the results are small.
Guidance belongs to Allah: not even a prophet’s own son is guaranteed.
Ties of faith count more than ties of blood.

stories.title: Hud and the people of ‘Ad
p: The people of ‘Ad were famed for their strength and for towering buildings. They forgot who gave them that strength and asked, "Who is mightier than us in power?" Hud, one of their own, told them to worship Allah and thank Him.

They called him foolish. Hud answered calmly: "I put my trust in Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but He holds it by the forelock." When their warning came, it was a roaring wind that blew for seven nights and eight days until the people lay like fallen palm trunks.
l: Strength and skill are gifts to be thanked for, not boasted about.
A believer can stay calm when others threaten, because his trust is in Allah.

stories.title: Salih and the she-camel
p: The people of Thamud carved homes into the mountains and lived in comfort. Salih called them to worship Allah. They asked for a sign, so Allah sent a she-camel with a share of the water on her day and the people’s on theirs. He told them not to harm her.
A group of them killed her anyway. Salih gave them three days, and then a mighty cry struck them and they were left lifeless in their homes.
l: A sign from Allah is a test of how we treat what we are given.
Comfort and technology do not protect a people who turn their backs on Allah.

stories.title: Ibrahim, the friend of Allah
p: Ibrahim searched for the truth by reason. He looked at a star, then the moon, then the sun, and set each aside because they set. He declared: "I have turned my face to the One who created the heavens and the earth." He asked his father and his people why they worshipped statues that could neither hear nor help.

One day when the town was away, he broke the idols and left the largest. When they asked who did it, he pointed to the big one and told them to ask it. They were stunned, then furious, and threw him into a great fire. Allah said: "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Ibrahim."

Later he left his wife Hajar and infant Ismail in a barren valley by Allah’s command, and was tested with the command to sacrifice his son. Both submitted, and Allah ransomed the boy with a great sacrifice. Together Ibrahim and Ismail raised the foundations of the Kaaba and prayed: "Our Lord, accept this from us."
l: Faith grows from honest reflection and then from complete submission.
When you obey Allah, He turns even fire into safety.
Make dua for what you build, and for the generations after you.

stories.title: Hajar, Ismail and Zamzam
p: Ibrahim left Hajar and baby Ismail in a valley with no people, water or plants, with only a bag of dates and a skin of water. When he turned to go, Hajar asked, "Did Allah command you to do this?" He said yes. She replied, "Then He will not let us be lost."

When the water ran out and her son cried with thirst, she ran seven times between the hills of Safa and Marwa, looking for help. Then she heard a voice, and at Ismail’s feet the spring of Zamzam appeared. A passing tribe, Jurhum, saw birds circling over water and settled there with her permission, and Makkah began.
This account is reported in Sahih al-Bukhari, narrated by Ibn ‘Abbas.
l: Her trust that Allah would not abandon her was met with a spring that still flows today.
The walking between Safa and Marwa in Hajj remembers a mother’s effort.
Do your part, and keep your trust in Allah.
stories.src: Sahih al-Bukhari (Ibn ‘Abbas); Qur’an 14:37

stories.title: Lut and the cities of the plain
p: Lut was sent to a people who openly committed a shameful act that no one before them had done. He warned them to fear Allah and reminded them that he asked for no reward.

They answered by threatening to expel him and his family for wanting to stay clean. Angels came in the form of guests, told Lut to leave with his believing family before dawn, and warned that his wife, who sided with the wrongdoers, would not be saved. Then the town was overturned and rained upon.
l: Calling people to what is right can bring hostility, but it is still a duty.
Being close to a righteous person does not save someone who chooses the other side.

stories.title: Yusuf, the best of stories
p: As a boy, Yusuf dreamed of eleven stars, the sun and the moon bowing to him. His father Ya’qub told him to keep it from his brothers, who were already jealous. They threw him into a well and told their father a wolf had eaten him. Ya’qub said, "Patience is beautiful."

A caravan found Yusuf and sold him in Egypt. In the household of a noble he grew up, and when the lady of the house tried to seduce him he said, "I seek refuge in Allah." He ran for the door and was falsely imprisoned instead. In prison he kept calling to Allah and interpreted dreams, and when the king dreamed of seven fat cows eaten by seven thin ones, Yusuf explained the coming famine and was made keeper of the stores.

Years later his brothers came for grain. He recognised them; they did not recognise him. When he revealed himself and they feared his reaction, he said, "No blame upon you today. May Allah forgive you." The dream of his childhood came true.
l: Beautiful patience trusts that Allah’s plan is bigger than the pit you are in.
Integrity under temptation is heroic, and Allah rewards it.
Forgiveness from a position of power is true nobility.
stories.src: Qur’an, Surah Yusuf (12) in full

stories.title: Ayyub and patience
p: Ayyub was a prophet who lost his health, his wealth and his family. For a long time he endured, never complaining against Allah. At last he called out quietly: "Indeed adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful."
Allah answered at once. He told him to strike the ground with his foot and drink and wash from the spring that appeared. Health returned, and Allah gave back his family and as many again.
l: Dua is not the opposite of patience. Ayyub made it while still patient.
Allah’s help can come from the very ground under your feet.

stories.title: Shu’ayb and honest trade
p: The people of Madyan cheated in business, giving short measure and weight. Shu’ayb told them: give full measure, do not spread corruption, and what Allah leaves you is better for you if you are believers.

They mocked his prayers and threatened to stone him. When their warning came, the earthquake found them in their homes. Shu’ayb left them with the words: "I conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and advised you."
l: Honesty in weights, prices and promises is part of worship.
Quick profit from cheating is not worth the loss of barakah.

stories.title: Musa and Fir’awn
p: Fir’awn was killing the newborn sons of Bani Israil. Musa’s mother was inspired to place her baby in a basket on the river and trust Allah, who promised to return him. He floated to Fir’awn’s own household, who adopted him, and his mother was brought back as his nurse.

As a young man, Musa struck a man who died and fled to Madyan. There he watered the flocks of two women without asking anything, then sat in the shade and said, "My Lord, I am in need of whatever good You send down to me." He worked for years for the women’s father and married.

On the way back, he saw a fire by the mountain. A voice told him: "I am your Lord." Allah gave him signs, including the staff, and sent him with his brother Harun to Fir’awn. After the magicians themselves believed, Fir’awn chased the Israelites to the sea, which Allah split. Musa and his people crossed; Fir’awn drowned.
l: Trust Allah with what you love most; He can return it better.
Helping others without asking for anything can be the key to your own provision.
No tyrant, however powerful, can overcome Allah’s plan.

stories.title: Dawud and Sulayman
p: A young Dawud faced the giant Jalut (Goliath) in battle and, by Allah’s permission, defeated him. Allah gave him kingship and the Zabur, made iron soft in his hands, and the mountains and birds joined him in praise. When he realised a case he judged had been a test, he asked forgiveness, fell down in prostration and turned back to Allah.

His son Sulayman was given command of wind and jinn, and understanding of the speech of birds and ants. Passing an ant colony, he smiled at the ant’s warning and prayed: "My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favour." When Bilqis, queen of Sheba, came to see his kingdom, she saw the truth in his message and submitted: "My Lord, I have wronged myself, and I submit with Sulayman to Allah."
l: Power in the hands of the thankful is a blessing; Dawud and Sulayman used it to turn back to Allah.
No creature is too small to deserve attention and care.

stories.title: Yunus in the belly of the fish
p: Yunus called his people, but when they would not respond he left them in anger, before Allah gave him permission. On a loaded ship, lots were drawn and he was thrown into the sea, and a great fish swallowed him.

In the darkness of the night, the sea and the fish’s belly, he called out: "There is no god but You. Glory to You. I was among the wrongdoers." Allah rescued him. His people, in the meantime, had believed, and Allah let them live in ease for a time.
l: Admit your mistake and return, even from the deepest dark.
This dua is reported to relieve distress (at-Tirmidhi), and Allah says He saves believers this way.
Do not give up on people. They may believe after you leave.

stories.title: Zakariyya and Yahya
p: Zakariyya was very old, his wife could not have children, and he feared for what would happen to the faith after him. Seeing the provision that appeared in Maryam’s prayer-room, he went and called quietly to his Lord: "My Lord, my bones have weakened and my hair is gray, yet never was I disappointed in my prayer to You."
The angels gave him news of a son, Yahya, whom Allah described as noble, chaste and a prophet from among the righteous.
l: No situation is too late for Allah’s mercy.
A quiet dua from the heart reaches Allah.

stories.title: Maryam and ‘Isa
p: Maryam was devoted to worship from childhood and raised in the care of Zakariyya. One day an angel came to her in human form and told her she would have a son, ‘Isa, with no father: it is easy for Allah, who says "Be" and it is.

In labour, alone beside a palm trunk, she cried in distress. A voice reassured her: shake the trunk, eat, drink and be comforted. When her people accused her, she pointed to the baby. He spoke in the cradle: "Indeed I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet."

‘Isa called to the worship of Allah, and by Allah’s permission healed the blind, healed the leper and gave life to the dead. The Qur’an says he was not killed or crucified: Allah raised him to Himself.
l: ‘Isa is among the greatest messengers, a servant of Allah.
When Maryam was most alone, Allah sent comfort and provision.
Trust and purity are rewarded in unexpected ways.

stories.title: The People of the Cave
p: A group of young men lived under a ruler who forced people to worship others besides Allah. They left their town and took refuge in a cave, praying: "Our Lord, grant us mercy from Yourself and prepare for us right guidance in our affair."

Allah caused them to sleep for years. When they woke, they thought it had been a day or part of a day. One went to buy food with an old coin, and the townspeople realised who they were. By then the people of the town had come to believe in Allah.
l: Protect your faith even if it means walking away from comfort.
Allah protects those who flee to Him.
stories.src: Qur’an 18:9–26. Surah al-Kahf is recommended on Fridays.

stories.title: Dhul-Qarnayn, the just ruler
p: Allah gave Dhul-Qarnayn power and a way to everything. He travelled to the west and the east, and he judged fairly: to those who wronged he gave punishment, and to those who believed and did good he gave good words and ease.

He met a people who said that Ya’juj and Ma’juj were spreading corruption, and asked him to build a barrier. He asked only for their strong hands, not payment, and built it from iron and molten copper. He said: "This is a mercy from my Lord."
l: Real power is serving people and giving credit to Allah.
He refused payment and asked for effort instead.

stories.title: Musa and al-Khidr
p: Musa was asked, "Who is the most knowledgeable?" and replied that it was he. Allah told him of a servant who had knowledge from Allah that he did not. Musa set out to meet him, and asked to follow him and learn. Al-Khidr told him he would not have the patience, but agreed on one condition: do not ask about anything until I explain.

The man damaged a boat. He struck down a boy. He rebuilt a wall for a town that refused them food. Musa could not hold his tongue each time. Finally Khidr explained: the boat belonged to poor men and a king was seizing good boats; the boy would have burdened his believing parents with disbelief; the wall protected the treasure of two orphans.
l: What looks like harm may hide mercy; we see only part of the picture.
Even a great prophet was humbled by the limits of his knowledge.
stories.src: Qur’an 18:60–82; the setting is in Sahih al-Bukhari

stories.title: Luqman’s advice to his son
p: Allah gave Luqman wisdom and told him to be grateful. He is remembered for the advice he gave his son: do not associate anything with Allah, for that is a great wrong; if a thing weighs as little as a mustard seed, hidden in a rock or in the heavens or earth, Allah will bring it forth.

He told his son to establish prayer, enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and be patient. He added: do not turn your cheek in contempt to people or walk the earth arrogantly, be moderate in your pace, and lower your voice.
l: Good character is part of wisdom.
Parents’ advice to children is a gift that should be recorded.

stories.title: Qarun and his treasures
p: Qarun was of the people of Musa but he was arrogant. Allah gave him so many treasures that its keys alone were a burden for a group of strong men. His people told him: do not exult, seek the home of the Hereafter through what Allah gave you, and do good as Allah has done good to you.

He answered, "I was given it only because of knowledge I have." When he came out before the people in splendour, those who wanted worldly life wished for what he had. Then Allah caused the earth to swallow him and his house.
l: Wealth is a test. Credit for it belongs to Allah.
What looked enviable can vanish, and those who valued knowledge of Allah were right.

stories.title: The Owners of the Garden
p: The Qur’an tells of owners of a rich garden. They swore they would pick its fruit early in the morning, and they agreed that no poor person should enter it that day. They did not say "if Allah wills."

During the night, a calamity from Allah went over the garden while they slept. In the morning, they went to find it like a harvested field. Then the most just of them said, "Did I not tell you to glorify Allah?" They said, "Glory to our Lord, we were wrongdoers," and turned to Allah in regret.
l: Charity is a right of the poor on your wealth.
Say "if Allah wills" over every plan.

stories.title: The Year of the Elephant
p: Abraha, the Abyssinian governor of Yemen, built a great church and wanted the Arabs to make pilgrimage there instead of the Kaaba. He marched on Makkah with an army and elephants. The Quraysh, unable to face him, moved to the hills, and ‘Abd al-Muttalib told him the House has a Lord who protects it.
When the army turned to enter, flocks of birds appeared, dropping hard clay stones on it, and left it like eaten straw. That year, around 570 CE, is when the Prophet ﷺ was born.
l: Allah protects His sacred House.
The year of Muhammad’s ﷺ birth began with a sign against arrogance.
stories.src: Qur’an, Surah al-Fil (105)

stories.title: The Boy, the King and the Trench
p: Allah mentions the People of the Trench in Surah al-Buruj, and the Prophet ﷺ told the full story, in Sahih Muslim (narrated by Suhayb). A king had a sorcerer, who, as he aged, was given a boy to train. On the way the boy met a monk and secretly learned the truth about Allah.

The boy healed the blind and the sick, and said, "I do not heal; Allah heals." When the king found out he killed the monk and tried to kill the boy several times, but failed. The boy told the king how he could be killed: gather the people, take an arrow from my quiver, and say "In the name of Allah, the Lord of this boy." The king did so, and the boy died. The people shouted, "We believe in the Lord of the boy!"

Furious, the king dug trenches and lit fires, throwing those who would not renounce their faith into them. When a woman with her baby hesitated, the baby spoke: "Be patient, mother, for you are on the truth."
l: Faith can spread through the courage of one young person.
The believers’ steadfastness is valued by Allah more than their survival.
stories.src: Sahih Muslim (Suhayb); Qur’an 85:4–10

stories.title: The Believer from Pharaoh’s Household
p: When Fir’awn threatened to kill Musa, a man from his own household, who had hidden his faith, spoke out: "Would you kill a man because he says, My Lord is Allah, when he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord?"

He warned them with the fate of earlier peoples, called them to the path of right guidance, and said: "I entrust my affair to Allah." Allah protected him from what they plotted, and Fir’awn’s people were struck by the worst punishment.
l: Speak the truth where you are, even in the most difficult setting.
Trusting Allah protects from harm in ways we cannot see.

stories.title: The Man from the Edge of the City
p: Messengers came to a town and its people rejected them. A man came running from the far end of the city: "O my people, follow the messengers! Follow those who ask no payment and who are rightly guided."

They killed him. Allah said to him, "Enter Paradise," and he said: "If only my people knew how my Lord has forgiven me and made me among the honoured." He is remembered for wishing them good even after what they did.
l: One person can speak up when others stay silent.
A believer’s heart stays kind even to those who harmed him.

stories.title: Talut, Jalut and young Dawud
p: Bani Israil asked their prophet for a king to lead them in battle. Allah appointed Talut. They objected that he lacked wealth, but the prophet said Allah gave him knowledge and strength in body. As the army set out, Talut tested them with a river: those who drank little were with him; those who drank much were not.

When they faced Jalut’s great army, even the believers said, "We have no power today." But those who were sure they would meet Allah said, "How many a small group has overcome a large one by Allah’s permission!" Dawud killed Jalut, and Allah gave him kingship.
l: Victory comes from Allah, not numbers.
Obedience and discipline matter before the battle.

stories.title: The Man of the Two Gardens
p: Two men: one had two gardens of grapevines and palms with a river running between, and boasted to his friend, "I am greater than you in wealth and mightier in manpower." He said he doubted the Hour would come.

His friend, a believer, told him: "When you entered your garden, why did you not say, What Allah wills; there is no power except with Allah?" Soon the gardens were destroyed, and the man wrung his hands in regret over what he had spent on them.
l: Say "Masha Allah, la quwwata illa billah" when you see blessings.
What you own can be gone overnight; faith is the only wealth that stays.

stories.title: Birth and orphanhood
p: Muhammad ﷺ was born in Makkah in the Year of the Elephant, to ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib and Aminah bint Wahb of the tribe of Quraysh. His father had died before his birth. As was the custom, he was sent to a wet-nurse in the desert, Halimah of Banu Sa’d, where the air was clean and he learned pure Arabic.

His mother died when he was about six, and his grandfather ‘Abd al-Muttalib took him in. When his grandfather died two years later, his uncle Abu Talib became his guardian. The Qur’an reminds him: "Did He not find you an orphan and give you refuge?"
l: The final Messenger knew loss early and understood the orphan.
Allah took care of him at every stage before the message came.
stories.src: Qur’an 93:6–8; Sira of Ibn Ishaq

stories.title: Al-Amin, the trustworthy
p: As a young man he tended sheep, and at about twelve travelled with Abu Talib to Syria, where, the biographies report, the monk Bahira noticed signs of prophethood in him. In Makkah he became so known for honesty that people called him al-Amin, the trustworthy, and left their valuables with him.

Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, a respected widow and merchant, hired him to trade for her. Impressed by his honesty and character, she proposed marriage. He was twenty-five. It was a loving marriage that lasted until her death.

When Quraysh rebuilt the Kaaba and quarrelled over who would set the Black Stone, it is reported that they agreed to accept the first man to enter. It was Muhammad. He laid the stone on a cloak and let each clan hold its edge, and so avoided a war.
l: His character was famous long before he preached.
Trust and honesty are the foundation of influence.
stories.src: Sira of Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Hisham

stories.title: The first revelation
stories.era: Ramadan, c. 610 CE, Cave of Hira
p: Troubled by the idolatry around him, he went to the cave of Hira above Makkah to reflect. In his fortieth year, the angel Jibril came and said, "Read!" He answered, "I cannot read." Jibril pressed him three times and said: "Read in the name of your Lord who created."

Shaken, he ran home to Khadijah: "Cover me!" She comforted him with words that history preserves: "Never! By Allah, Allah will never disgrace you. You keep family ties, you bear the burdens of the weak, you give to the poor, you honour the guest, and you help against hardships." She took him to her cousin Waraqah ibn Nawfal, who said: this is the same angel who came to Musa.
This is reported in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, narrated by ‘A’ishah.
l: Revelation began with "Read", with knowledge.
Khadijah recognised his goodness before she understood his mission.
stories.src: Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim (‘A’ishah); Qur’an 96:1–5

stories.title: The quiet call and the public call
p: For about three years he invited people privately. The first to believe were Khadijah, his young cousin ‘Ali, his freed servant Zayd ibn Harithah, and his close friend Abu Bakr, who brought others. They met at the house of al-Arqam.

When he was commanded to warn his closest relatives, he climbed Mount Safa and called out to Quraysh. When they gathered he asked: "If I told you an army was behind this mountain, would you believe me?" They said: "We have never known you to lie." He then warned them of a severe punishment. His uncle Abu Lahab cursed him, and Surah al-Masad was revealed about him.
l: He began with those who knew him best, and they believed.
Even those who rejected him admitted he never lied.
stories.src: Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim (Safa); Sira

stories.title: Persecution in Makkah
p: As the call spread, Quraysh turned to mockery and then to torture, mainly against the weak. Bilal was dragged over the hot sand with a rock on his chest, repeating "Ahad, Ahad" (One, One). Sumayyah and her husband Yasir were killed, becoming the first martyrs of Islam. Khabbab was burned on hot coals.

When Khabbab complained, the Prophet ﷺ reminded him of earlier believers who were sawn in two and combed with iron combs, and said Allah would complete this matter until a traveller could ride from Sana’a to Hadramawt fearing only Allah (Sahih al-Bukhari).
l: Faith was never promised to be free of hardship.
Steadfastness under torture became the foundation of the community.
stories.src: Sahih al-Bukhari (Khabbab); Sira

stories.title: Refuge in Abyssinia
p: With the persecution worsening, the Prophet ﷺ told some Muslims to go to Abyssinia, where, he said, there was a king under whom no one is wronged. A small group left first, then a larger one, about eighty, led by Ja’far ibn Abi Talib.

Quraysh sent envoys with gifts to bring them back. The Negus, the Christian king, asked the Muslims about their faith. Ja’far explained how Islam had changed them and recited the opening of Surah Maryam. The Negus wept. He said that what they recited and what ‘Isa brought came from the same lamp, and refused to hand them over. (As reported in the Sira.)
l: Protect your faith and your people, even by leaving.
Truth can win a fair-minded listener in a different land.
stories.src: Sira of Ibn Ishaq and Musnad Ahmad

stories.title: The boycott and the Year of Sorrow
p: Quraysh agreed to boycott the Prophet’s ﷺ clan, Banu Hashim, refusing trade or marriage with them. For about three years his family endured hunger in a valley, the Shi’b of Abu Talib. It ended when some of Quraysh themselves cancelled the pact.

Soon afterwards, in the same year, both his uncle Abu Talib, who had protected him, and his wife Khadijah died. It became known as the Year of Sorrow. Without his protector, the persecution grew harder.
l: Even the Prophet ﷺ lost those closest to him.
Grief and patience belong together.
stories.src: Sira of Ibn Ishaq

stories.title: Ta’if: the hardest day
p: Seeking support, he went to the town of Ta’if. Its leaders rejected him, mocked him and sent their children and servants to pelt him with stones until his feet bled. He sheltered in an orchard, deeply hurt.

‘A’ishah once asked him if any day was harder than Uhud. He said that the worst he had suffered was at ‘Aqabah on that day. On his way back, he looked up and saw a cloud with Jibril in it, and the angel of the mountains who said: "If you wish, I will close the two mountains on them." He answered: "No. I hope that Allah will bring from their descendants people who worship Allah alone." (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim)
l: At his lowest moment he chose mercy.
He looked to the future generation, not the present anger.
stories.src: Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim (‘A’ishah)

stories.title: Al-Isra’ wal-Mi’raj
p: In one night Allah took His servant from the Sacred Mosque in Makkah to al-Aqsa in Jerusalem, and then raised him through the heavens, meeting earlier prophets. He saw Jibril in his true form at the Lote-Tree of the Boundary.

On that night, the prayers were prescribed: first fifty a day. On the way back, Musa advised him to ask for a reduction, again and again, until it was five. Allah said they are five in number but fifty in reward. (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim)
l: The prayer was given directly, on a night of comfort after hardship.
Five prayers carry the reward of fifty.
stories.src: Qur’an 17:1, 53:1–18; Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim

stories.title: The pledges at ‘Aqabah
p: Each pilgrimage season the Prophet ﷺ met tribes. Six men from Yathrib (later Madinah) believed, then a dozen came the next year and pledged not to associate anything with Allah, steal or commit adultery. He sent Mus’ab ibn ‘Umayr with them to teach the Qur’an, and Islam spread in nearly every house in Yathrib.
The next year, over seventy people came and pledged to protect him as they would their own families. The path to Hijrah was open.
l: Quiet teaching by one dedicated person can change a city.
The Ansar pledged protection when others had closed their doors.
stories.src: Sira of Ibn Ishaq; Musnad Ahmad

stories.title: The Hijrah
p: Quraysh agreed to have one man from each clan strike him together. The night they came, ‘Ali slept in his bed. The Prophet ﷺ left home with Abu Bakr, reciting the opening of Ya-Sin, and hid in the cave of Thawr. Abu Bakr’s daughter Asma’ carried them food, and tore her waist-belt in two for the bags, earning the name "She of the two belts."

When the pursuers reached the mouth of the cave, Abu Bakr whispered, "If one of them looks down at his feet, he will see us." The Prophet ﷺ answered: "What do you think of two when Allah is their third?" (Sahih al-Bukhari). The Qur’an records it: "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us."
After days of travel they reached Quba, then Madinah, where the people came out to welcome him. This journey marks the start of the Islamic calendar.
l: Plan carefully, then trust Allah completely.
Real companionship is being willing to be in danger with someone.
stories.src: Qur’an 9:40; Sahih al-Bukhari (Abu Bakr); Sira

stories.title: Building Madinah
p: His first act in Madinah was to build a mosque, working with the Companions carrying bricks. It was a place of prayer, learning and community. Then he paired Muhajirun (emigrants) with Ansar (helpers) as brothers. Sa’d ibn al-Rabi’ offered his brother ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf half his wealth and even to choose a wife. ‘Abd al-Rahman replied, "May Allah bless you in your family and wealth. Show me the market," and began trading. (Sahih al-Bukhari)

The Prophet ﷺ also agreed a charter with the Jewish tribes and others in Madinah, known as the Constitution of Madinah, establishing mutual defence and rights. The adhan was introduced, and Bilal became the first caller to prayer.
l: A community starts with a place to gather and a bond of brotherhood.
Generosity on one side and dignity on the other: he asked for the market, not a handout.
stories.src: Sahih al-Bukhari (‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf); Sira

stories.title: Badr
p: About 313 Muslims with few horses and a handful of camels met a Quraysh army of nearly a thousand at the wells of Badr. The night before, the Prophet ﷺ spent the night in prayer and rain fell. In the battle, the Muslims won decisively. Allah says He helped them although they were few.

It is known as the Day of Criterion (Furqan), the day truth and falsehood were separated. After the battle, the prisoners were treated kindly, and some of those who could write were reportedly freed in exchange for teaching Muslim children to write.
l: Victory is from Allah, though effort is required.
Treat prisoners with mercy.

stories.title: Uhud
p: The Muslims, around seven hundred, faced about three thousand. The Prophet ﷺ placed fifty archers on a hill and told them not to leave their position whatever happened. When the Muslims began to win, most of the archers left for the spoils. Quraysh cavalry circled behind, and the tide turned.

The Prophet ﷺ was wounded. Seventy Muslims were killed, including his uncle Hamza. Allah consoled them in Surah Al ‘Imran: "Do not weaken and do not grieve, and you will be superior if you are believers," and reminded them that the loss came from a failure to obey a command (Sahih al-Bukhari).
l: Obedience to the leader’s clear instruction matters more than personal calculation.
Even a defeat is a lesson and a mercy.
stories.src: Qur’an 3:121–175; Sahih al-Bukhari (the archers)

stories.title: The Trench
p: A coalition of Arab tribes, about ten thousand, marched on Madinah. Salman al-Farisi, a Persian, is reported to have suggested digging a trench, a defence unknown to the Arabs. The Companions dug it in freezing weather, hungry, with the Prophet ﷺ digging beside them and tying a stone to his stomach against hunger (Sahih al-Bukhari).

For weeks the armies sat on either side of it, until a cold wind and storm broke their camp, and they left. The Qur’an remembers how the believers were shaken, then said: "This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us."
l: Good ideas can come from anyone.
Leaders share the hardship.
stories.src: Qur’an 33:9–27; Sahih al-Bukhari

stories.title: Al-Hudaybiyyah: a clear victory
p: The Prophet ﷺ set out with about fourteen hundred Companions in a state of ihram to perform ‘umrah. Quraysh stopped them at Hudaybiyyah. After tense talks, a treaty was agreed with terms that seemed unfair, such as sending back anyone fleeing Makkah to join the Muslims. Many Companions, including ‘Umar, were upset.

He told them to sacrifice and shave their heads, and no one moved. His wife Umm Salamah advised: go out and do it yourself without speaking to anyone. When he did, they followed. Allah then revealed Surah al-Fath: "Indeed We have given you a clear conquest." The truce let Islam spread in peace, and the early historians note that more people entered Islam in the following two years than in all the years before. (The sacrifice and Umm Salamah’s advice are in Sahih al-Bukhari.)
l: What looks like a setback may open the way.
Lead by doing, and listen to good counsel.
stories.src: Qur’an 48; Sahih al-Bukhari

stories.title: Letters to the rulers
p: After Hudaybiyyah, the Prophet ﷺ sent letters to the rulers of the time: Heraclius of Byzantium, Khosrow of Persia, the Negus of Abyssinia, the Muqawqis of Egypt and others, inviting them to Islam. The letter to Heraclius is quoted in Sahih al-Bukhari: "Peace be upon whoever follows guidance. Accept Islam and you will be safe..."

Heraclius asked questions of Abu Sufyan, then still an opponent, about the Prophet’s lineage, truthfulness and followers, and judged these to be signs of a prophet. The Negus accepted Islam. Khosrow tore up the letter.
l: The message was meant for all humanity.
Even his enemy Abu Sufyan could not deny his truthfulness.
stories.src: Sahih al-Bukhari (letter to Heraclius); Sira

stories.title: Mu’tah
p: A Muslim envoy was killed by a Byzantine ally, so the Prophet ﷺ sent an army of three thousand under Zayd ibn Harithah, saying: if Zayd is killed, Ja’far takes command, and if Ja’far is killed, ‘Abdullah ibn Rawahah. They faced a force many times larger. All three commanders fell in turn.

In Madinah, the Prophet ﷺ told the people of their deaths with tears in his eyes, before the news reached them. Khalid ibn al-Walid then took the banner, and was called "a sword among the swords of Allah." (Sahih al-Bukhari)
l: Leaders led from the front and died for what they believed.
The community kept going when its leaders fell.
stories.src: Sahih al-Bukhari

stories.title: The Conquest of Makkah
p: After Quraysh broke the treaty, the Prophet ﷺ marched on Makkah with ten thousand. He entered with his head bowed so low it nearly touched his camel, in thankfulness. He cleaned the Kaaba of its idols, saying: "The truth has come, and falsehood has vanished."

The people who had persecuted, boycotted and driven him out awaited his verdict. As reported in the Sira, he asked: "What do you think I will do with you?" They said: "Good. You are a noble brother, son of a noble brother." He said: "Go, for you are free." Bilal climbed the Kaaba and called the adhan. Surah an-Nasr was soon revealed.
l: Victory was met with humility and pardon, not revenge.
Mercy won more hearts than force.
stories.src: Qur’an 17:81, 110; Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim (the Kaaba); Sira

stories.title: Hunayn and the Ansar
p: At Hunayn, the Muslims, now twelve thousand, felt confident in their numbers and were caught in an ambush. For a moment many fled, until the Prophet ﷺ called them back and they recovered. The Qur’an says: "Your great number did not avail you."

In the distribution of the spoils, he gave generously to new Muslims, to win their hearts. Some Ansar felt hurt. He gathered them and said: "Are you not content that the people go with sheep and camels while you return with the Messenger of Allah to your homes?" They wept until their beards were wet and said: "We are content." (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim)
l: Numbers do not decide victory.
He made loyal people feel valued, and they were moved to tears.
stories.src: Qur’an 9:25–26; Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim

stories.title: Tabuk and the three who stayed behind
p: The Prophet ﷺ called the Muslims to march in the heat of summer against the Byzantines at Tabuk. Wealthy Companions gave large amounts, including ‘Uthman, who equipped much of the army, and Abu Bakr, who gave everything he owned.

Three Companions, Ka’b ibn Malik, Murarah ibn al-Rabi’ and Hilal ibn Umayyah, stayed behind without a valid excuse. When the Prophet ﷺ returned, the hypocrites made excuses; Ka’b chose to tell the truth. The three were shunned by the community for fifty days, until Allah accepted their repentance. Ka’b said that truthfulness was the reason he was saved, and he promised never to lie again. (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim)
l: Honest repentance, even when hard, is the way out.
The community can hold its members accountable and still welcome them back.
stories.src: Qur’an 9:117–119; Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim (Ka’b ibn Malik)

stories.title: The Farewell Pilgrimage
p: In his only Hajj, with over a hundred thousand Muslims, he stood at Arafah and gave a sermon. As recorded in Sahih Muslim (Jabir): your blood and your wealth are sacred, like the sanctity of this day, this month and this city; all interest from the Days of Ignorance is cancelled; fear Allah regarding women, for you have rights over them and they have rights over you; and "I have left among you something that, if you hold to it, you will never go astray: the Book of Allah."

He asked the people: "Have I conveyed the message?" They answered: "Yes." He raised his finger to the sky and said: "O Allah, be witness." On that Arafah, the verse was revealed: "This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favour upon you."
l: Human life, property and dignity are sacred.
Hold on to the Qur’an.
stories.src: Sahih Muslim (Jabir); Sahih al-Bukhari; Qur’an 5:3

stories.title: His passing
p: He fell ill and, with the permission of his wives, stayed in ‘A’ishah’s house. As he grew weaker, he asked Abu Bakr to lead the prayer. He is reported to have urged, near the end, "the prayer, and those under your care." He passed away on a Monday with his head on ‘A’ishah’s chest (Sahih al-Bukhari).

The Companions were stunned; ‘Umar could not believe it. Abu Bakr entered, kissed him, then went out and said: "Whoever worshipped Muhammad, Muhammad has died. Whoever worships Allah, Allah is Ever-Living and does not die." He recited: "Muhammad is no more than a messenger; messengers have passed before him." The people felt as if they had never heard it before. (Sahih al-Bukhari)
l: The Prophet was human, and the message is for Allah alone.
Abu Bakr’s steadiness held the community together.
stories.src: Sahih al-Bukhari (‘A’ishah, Abu Bakr); Qur’an 3:144

stories.title: Khadijah, the first believer
p: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid was a successful businesswoman, known in Makkah as "the pure one". She hired Muhammad ﷺ to trade for her, proposed to him, and was his wife for about twenty-five years. When revelation came and he was frightened, she was the first person to believe in him.

She spent her wealth in support of Islam, stood by him in the boycott, and the Prophet ﷺ remembered her with love all his life. Jibril conveyed Allah’s greetings to her, with news of a house in Paradise (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim).
l: Support at the right moment can change history.
Faith and generosity go together.
stories.src: Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim; Sira

stories.title: Abu Bakr as-Siddiq
p: Abu Bakr was the first man outside the family to believe, and he never hesitated: when told about the Isra’ and Mi’raj he is reported to have said, "If he said it, it is true." That is the origin of his title as-Siddiq, "the one who affirms the truth."

He bought and freed enslaved Muslims such as Bilal. He was the Prophet’s ﷺ companion in the cave. When the army was equipped for Tabuk, he brought everything he owned, and when asked what he had left for his family, said: "Allah and His Messenger." After the Prophet’s ﷺ death he steadied the community and became the first caliph.
l: Belief without delay and sacrifice without counting.
Calm in crisis: his words at the Prophet’s death held people together.
stories.src: Sahih al-Bukhari; Sunan Abi Dawud and at-Tirmidhi (Tabuk gift); Sira

stories.title: ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab
p: ‘Umar was known for his strength and was at first a harsh opponent. As reported in the Sira, he set out to find the Prophet ﷺ and heard that his own sister had accepted Islam. Finding her reading from Surah Ta-Ha, he asked to read it, and his heart softened. He went to the Prophet ﷺ and accepted Islam.

‘Abdullah ibn Mas’ud said: "We have been strong since ‘Umar became Muslim" (Sahih al-Bukhari), as Muslims could now pray openly at the Kaaba. As the second caliph he was known for justice, for patrolling at night to check on the poor, and for expanding the Muslim state.
l: A heart can change when it meets the Qur’an.
Strength is best used for justice.
stories.src: Sahih al-Bukhari; Sira

stories.title: Bilal ibn Rabah
p: Bilal was an Abyssinian slave in Makkah whose master tortured him for believing, laying a rock on his chest in the midday heat. He kept saying "Ahad, Ahad." Abu Bakr bought and freed him.

In Madinah he became the first mu’adhdhin. The Prophet ﷺ once told him: "Bilal, tell me about the deed you did in Islam that you hope most for, for I heard the sound of your footsteps ahead of me in Paradise." Bilal said: "I do not do anything greater than this, that whenever I make wudu, day or night, I pray with that wudu what Allah has written for me." (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). At the conquest of Makkah, he called the adhan from the Kaaba.
l: Worth in Islam is faith and deeds, not origin or status.
A small consistent habit raised him high.
stories.src: Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim; Sira

stories.title: ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib
p: ‘Ali was raised in the Prophet’s ﷺ household and was among the first to accept Islam as a boy. On the night of the Hijrah he slept in the Prophet’s ﷺ bed, to deceive those waiting outside to kill him.

At Khaybar the Prophet ﷺ said: "Tomorrow I will give the banner to a man who loves Allah and His Messenger, and whom Allah and His Messenger love." The next morning it was given to ‘Ali, and by Allah’s help the fortress fell (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). Known for his knowledge, courage and eloquence, he became the fourth caliph.
l: Faith from childhood, courage when it counts.
Trust of the Prophet was earned by deeds.
stories.src: Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim; Sira

stories.title: ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan
p: ‘Uthman was a wealthy, modest and shy man, so much so that the Prophet ﷺ said even the angels are shy of him (Sahih Muslim). He was twice the Prophet’s ﷺ son-in-law. When Madinah lacked a good water source, he bought the well of Rumah and made it free for all; at Tabuk he equipped a large part of the army.
As the third caliph, he had the Qur’an copied into standard volumes and sent to the main cities, preserving its unity for all later generations (Sahih al-Bukhari).
l: Wealth used for the community is a lasting charity.
He protected the Book for everyone who came after.
stories.src: Sahih Muslim; Sahih al-Bukhari (copying the Qur’an); Sunan at-Tirmidhi (Tabuk)

stories.title: ‘A’ishah bint Abi Bakr
p: ‘A’ishah, the Prophet’s ﷺ wife, became one of the greatest scholars of her time. She narrated over two thousand hadith, and senior Companions came to her with questions of law and the Prophet’s ﷺ private conduct. She is remembered for correcting others when their memory slipped.
Asked about the Prophet’s ﷺ behaviour at home, she said he used to help his family with chores, and when it was time for prayer he would get up and go. (Sahih al-Bukhari)
l: Women have been teachers of religion from the very beginning.
Knowledge is preserved by those who live close to the source.
stories.src: Sahih al-Bukhari; Sira

stories.title: Mus’ab ibn ‘Umayr
p: Mus’ab was the best-dressed young man of Makkah, from a wealthy family who doted on him. When he accepted Islam, his family tried to force him back and took away his comforts, and he gave it all up.

The Prophet ﷺ chose him to teach the first Muslims of Madinah. Within a year, nearly every house had been touched by Islam. He was killed at Uhud, holding the banner. Khabbab said that when he died, he left only a striped cloak: if they covered his head, his feet showed, and if they covered his feet, his head showed. (Sahih al-Bukhari)
l: Comfort was exchanged for the cause.
One well-prepared teacher can open a whole city.
stories.src: Sahih al-Bukhari; Sira

stories.title: Sumayyah bint Khayyat
p: Sumayyah and her husband Yasir and their son ‘Ammar were among the early believers without tribal protection. The Prophet ﷺ passed them while they were being tortured and said: "Be patient, family of Yasir, for your meeting place is Paradise."
As reported in the Sira, Abu Jahl killed Sumayyah when she would not renounce her faith, so she became the first martyr in Islam.
l: Faith is not dependent on tribe or power.
Her steadfastness is remembered more than any of her persecutors.
stories.src: Sira of Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Sa’d

stories.title: Salman the Persian
p: Salman grew up in a Zoroastrian family in Persia and left to seek the truth. He lived with Christian monks in Syria and Iraq, each pointing him to the next, until one told him the awaited prophet would appear in Arabia. On the way he was sold into slavery, and ended in Madinah.

There, he recognised the signs he had been told about and accepted Islam. After being freed, he gave the idea of digging the trench at the Battle of the Trench. (As reported in the Sira and Musnad Ahmad.)
l: A lifelong search ended in the truth.
A newcomer’s idea can save the whole community.
stories.src: Sira; Musnad Ahmad

stories.title: ‘Abdullah ibn Mas’ud and the Qur’an
p: Ibn Mas’ud was a young shepherd who became one of the great reciters. Early in Makkah, he asked to recite the Qur’an aloud in front of Quraysh at the Kaaba; they beat him, but he went again the next day. (As reported in the Sira.)

The Prophet ﷺ once asked him to recite to him. He said, "Shall I recite to you when it was revealed to you?" He replied, "I love to hear it from someone else." When Ibn Mas’ud reached the verse "How will it be when We bring from every nation a witness...", the Prophet ﷺ said "Enough," and his eyes were flowing with tears. (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim)
l: Courage to recite openly, and the humility to listen.
The Qur’an moved even the one who received it.
stories.src: Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim; Sira

stories.title: Umm Sulaym and her dowry
p: Abu Talhah proposed to Umm Sulaym, a widow with a son (Anas), before he became Muslim. She said: "A man like you is not turned down, but you are a disbeliever and I am a Muslim, and it is not lawful for me to marry you. If you become Muslim, that will be my dowry, and I ask nothing else."
He accepted Islam and they married. Thabit, one of the narrators, said he had never heard of a dowry better than hers. (an-Nasa’i, graded sound)
l: Faith valued above wealth or status.
A dignified and clear-minded woman changed a man’s life.
stories.src: Sunan an-Nasa’i

stories.title: The man who urinated in the mosque
p: A Bedouin stood and began to urinate in the mosque. The Companions rushed at him, but the Prophet ﷺ said: "Leave him, and pour a bucket of water over where he urinated. You were sent to make things easy, not to make them hard."

He then called the man and explained gently that mosques are not for urine or filth, but for the remembrance of Allah, prayer and the recitation of the Qur’an. (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, narrated by Anas)
l: Teach with gentleness: hearts open to kindness.
Prevent harm, but do not humiliate.
stories.src: Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim

stories.title: Kissing his grandson
p: The Prophet ﷺ kissed his grandson al-Hasan. Al-Aqra’ ibn Habis, a chieftain, who was sitting there said: "I have ten children and have never kissed any of them." The Prophet ﷺ looked at him and said: "Whoever does not show mercy will not be shown mercy." (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim)
l: Affection is part of the faith, not weakness.
Mercy toward children is a duty.
stories.src: Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim

stories.title: The woman at the grave
p: The Prophet ﷺ passed a woman weeping at a grave and told her: "Fear Allah and be patient." Not recognising him, she snapped: "Go away, you are not stricken with my calamity." When she was told it was the Prophet ﷺ, she went to his door and found no doorkeeper. She said: "I did not recognise you." He said: "Patience is at the first stroke of the calamity." (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim)
l: He accepted harsh words from someone in pain, without anger.
The reward is for the patience shown at the first moment.
stories.src: Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim (Anas)

stories.title: Standing for a funeral
p: A funeral procession passed by, and the Prophet ﷺ stood up. Told that it was the funeral of a Jewish man, he said: "Is it not a soul?" (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim)
l: Every human life deserves respect.
Death is a reminder, whoever it is.
stories.src: Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim

stories.title: Usamah and the man who said the shahadah
p: In a raid, Usamah ibn Zayd and an Ansari man caught a fleeing enemy. As Usamah raised his sword, the man said: "La ilaha illallah." Usamah struck and killed him anyway. When the Prophet ﷺ heard, he said: "Did you kill him after he said La ilaha illallah?" Usamah explained that the man said it only to save himself. The Prophet ﷺ kept repeating: "Did you split his heart open to know that?" Usamah said he wished he had not been Muslim before that day. (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim)
l: We judge what we see, and leave hearts to Allah.
Shedding blood is a very grave matter.
stories.src: Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim

stories.title: Ten years of service
p: Anas ibn Malik served the Prophet ﷺ from the age of about ten for ten years. He said: "I served him for ten years. He never said ‘uff’ to me, never asked why I did something, and never asked why I did not do something." (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim)
‘A’ishah said he never struck anything with his hand, neither a servant nor a woman, except in the cause of Allah (Sahih Muslim).
l: Patience with those under your care.
Good character is the best argument for the faith.
stories.src: Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim

stories.title: The Christians of Najran in his mosque
p: A delegation of Christians from Najran came to Madinah to meet the Prophet ﷺ. They discussed faith with him, and when their time of prayer came, he let them pray in his mosque. (As reported in the Sira, by Ibn Ishaq.)
The Qur’an records the discussion about ‘Isa and invites them to a common word: that we worship none but Allah and associate nothing with Him.
l: Dignity and hospitality towards guests of other faiths.
The invitation was to common ground.
stories.src: Sira of Ibn Ishaq; Qur’an 3:59–64

stories.title: Ishaq and Ya’qub
p: Angels who visited Ibrahim brought him good news of a son, Ishaq, whose mother Sarah was elderly. Ishaq’s son was Ya’qub, also called Isra’il, from whom Bani Isra’il take their name, and whose twelve sons became its tribes.
Ya’qub is remembered for his "beautiful patience" when Yusuf was lost, and for his last words to his sons: "What will you worship after me?"
l: A promise from Allah can arrive when every ordinary expectation has gone.
Patience that does not complain to people, only to Allah, is "beautiful".
A believer’s last concern is that his children keep the faith.

stories.title: Harun, the helper of Musa
p: Musa asked Allah for his brother Harun as a minister because he was more eloquent. Harun was with him before Fir’awn and was left in charge when Musa went to Mount Sinai.

While Musa was away, al-Samiri fashioned a calf from the people’s jewellery and many worshipped it. Harun warned them and, when Musa returned in anger and seized his brother’s head, said: "O son of my mother, the people overpowered me, and they were about to kill me."
l: A good helper can be a greater gift than a good talent.
Leadership sometimes means choosing unity and caution over confrontation; Harun explained and Musa accepted.
Even the nearest to a prophet can be tested by his own people.

stories.title: The two sons of Adam
p: Two sons of Adam each offered a sacrifice. Allah accepted one’s and not the other’s. The one rejected threatened to kill his brother. The righteous one said: "If you should raise your hand against me to kill me, I would not raise mine against you to kill you. Indeed I fear Allah." Then the brother killed him.

Not knowing what to do with the body, he watched a raven scratch the earth to show how to bury a body, and said: "Woe to me! Am I not able to be like this raven?" He was left among those full of regret.
l: Allah accepts what is sincere; envy is blind to that.
Self-restraint is stronger than retaliation.
The Prophet ﷺ said every unjust killing carries a share of sin for the first murderer, since he began the practice.
stories.src: Qur’an 5:27–32; Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim (the first murder)

stories.title: The people of Saba’ and the flood
p: The people of Saba’ in Yemen lived between two gardens, one to the right and one to the left of their land. They were told to eat from their Lord’s provision and to be grateful. They turned away.

Allah sent upon them the flood of the dam (sayl al-‘arim) and replaced their gardens with bitter fruit, tamarisk and a few lote trees. They had even asked that their journeys between towns be made longer.
l: Gratitude keeps blessings; neglect lets them go.
A people can have beauty, safety and trade, and lose everything by arrogance.
"Make longer the distances between our journeys" is a picture of discontent that has lost its gratitude.

stories.title: The Cow of Bani Isra’il
p: A man among Bani Isra’il was found murdered and each party blamed another. Musa told them that Allah commands them to slaughter a cow. They answered, "Do you take us in ridicule?" Then they began asking questions: what kind, what colour, what age, until the description became so narrow that they found only one.
Allah told them to strike the dead man with a part of the cow, and the dead man was brought back to life (the commentaries say, to name his killer). The surah is named for this story.
l: Obey the command as given. The more they questioned, the harder it became.
Allah shows how He gives life to the dead.
The Prophet ﷺ warned against excessive questions, "for they were destroyed by their many questions" (Sahih Muslim).

stories.title: The Table from Heaven
p: The disciples of ‘Isa asked whether his Lord could send down a table from the sky. ‘Isa told them to fear Allah if they were believers. They said they wished to eat from it, so their hearts would be at ease and they would know that he had told them the truth.
‘Isa prayed, and Allah said He would send it down, with a warning: whoever disbelieves after it will receive a punishment that He has not given to anyone in the worlds.
l: Asking for a sign after faith is a risk, because the responsibility becomes greater.
The dua of ‘Isa asks that the day be an Eid and a sign: gratitude is a part of every blessing.
The surah is named after this table (al-Ma’idah).

stories.title: The man who passed a ruined town
p: A man passed a town whose roofs had fallen in and asked, "How will Allah give this life after its death?" Allah caused him to die for a hundred years, then raised him.
