facts: After the expedition of al-Muraysi’ (Banu al-Mustaliq), 5 or 6 AH
‘Abdullah ibn Ubayy led it; a few believers repeated it, including Mistah, Hassan and Hamnah

t: ‘A’ishah’s own account (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim): the Prophet ﷺ used to draw lots among his wives when he travelled, and on this journey it was her turn. She was carried in a covered howdah. On the return, near Madinah, as the army camped at night, she went to relieve herself and found that her necklace of Zafar beads had fallen. She went back to look for it. The men who carried the howdah, believing she was inside since she was light, lifted it and moved on.

She came back to an empty camp, wrapped herself in her cloak and sat down, thinking they would come back for her. She fell asleep. Safwan ibn al-Mu’attal, who had been lagging behind the army, saw her, recognised her, as he had seen her before the hijab was revealed, and said "Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji’un." She woke, covered her face, and he made his camel kneel for her to mount, and led it on foot till they reached the army at midday.

‘Abdullah ibn Ubayy was seen spreading the story, and some Muslims, including Hassan ibn Thabit, Mistah ibn Uthathah and Hamnah bint Jahsh, joined in the talk. ‘A’ishah fell ill after returning and was not aware of what was being said. She noticed only that the Prophet ﷺ was less gentle than usual. When she went to her mother’s house, she heard from a woman what people were saying, and her illness doubled. She wept for days and nights.

The Prophet ﷺ consulted ‘Ali and Usamah. Usamah spoke well of her, and ‘Ali said that Allah had not constrained him and that there were many other women; ask the servant girl Barirah. Barirah said: "By the One who sent you with the truth, I have seen nothing in her except that she is a young girl who falls asleep over the dough and the goat eats it." He asked Zaynab bint Jahsh, who said: "I protect my hearing and sight; I know nothing about her except good." Aisha said that Zaynab was her rival among the wives but Allah protected her through her piety.

The Prophet ﷺ stood on the pulpit and asked: "Who will excuse me from a man who has harmed my family? By Allah, I know nothing but good about my family, and they have mentioned a man about whom I know only good." Sa’d ibn Mu’adh said that he would behead him if he were from Aws, and Sa’d ibn ‘Ubadah of Khazraj objected, and the tribes nearly came to blows, until the Prophet ﷺ calmed them.

He came to ‘A’ishah and said: "O ‘A’ishah, I have heard such and such about you. If you are innocent, Allah will declare your innocence; and if you have committed a sin, ask Allah’s forgiveness and repent, for when a servant admits his sin and repents, Allah accepts his repentance." Her tears dried up. She asked her parents to answer for her; they said they did not know what to say. She said: "I know that you have heard this and it has settled in your minds. If I say I am innocent, and Allah knows I am innocent, you will not believe me. If I admit to something Allah knows I did not do, you will believe me. I can only say what Yusuf’s father said: So patience is most fitting, and Allah is the One sought for help against what you describe." She turned over on her bed, and said: "I hoped Allah would show my innocence in a dream, but I did not think that revelation would be sent down about me."

Before anyone left, the Prophet ﷺ began to show the signs of revelation: sweat running down like pearls on a cold day. When it was over, he was smiling, and the first thing he said was: "O ‘A’ishah, Allah has declared your innocence." Her mother said, "Get up and go to him." She said: "By Allah, I will not get up to him, and I will not praise anyone but Allah." Then Allah revealed: "Indeed, those who came with falsehood are a group among you. Do not think it bad for you; rather it is good for you." (24:11) The ten verses continue to 24:20.

Abu Bakr had been supporting his poor relative Mistah ibn Uthathah. After Mistah spoke about ‘A’ishah, he swore he would never help him again. Allah revealed: "And let not those of virtue among you and wealth swear not to give [aid] to their relatives and the needy and the emigrants for the cause of Allah, and let them pardon and overlook. Would you not like that Allah should forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." (24:22) Abu Bakr said: "Yes, by Allah, I would like Allah to forgive me," and he resumed supporting Mistah, saying he would never stop it. (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim)
The punishment of eighty lashes was applied to some of those who had publicly accused her (Sunan Abi Dawud and al-Tirmidhi), as the law of qadhf requires four witnesses (24:4).

facts: 9 AH (630–631 CE), the Year of Delegations
Thaqif of Ta’if, Banu Tamim, ‘Abd al-Qays, Himyar, Najran
Led by Abu Bakr; ‘Ali announced the opening of Surah al-Tawbah

t: After the siege of Ta’if, ‘Urwah ibn Mas’ud al-Thaqafi, the man who had marvelled at the Companions at Hudaybiyyah, accepted Islam and went back to his people to call them. As he stood on his roof to invite them, he was shot and killed. Before dying, he forgave his killers and said it was a gift Allah had granted him. Later, in Ramadan 9 AH, the Thaqif sent a delegation to Madinah. They asked for conditions: that their idol al-Lat should be left for three years. The Prophet ﷺ refused, then every year, then a month. They finally accepted, and asked to be excused from prayer. He said: "There is no good in a religion without prayer." (as reported in the Sira and Sunan Abi Dawud). He appointed their youngest member, ‘Uthman ibn Abi al-‘As, who had asked to learn the Qur’an, as their leader. Al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah was sent to demolish al-Lat.

s.h: Banu Tamim and the pride of poets
t: The delegation of Banu Tamim arrived with their poet and orator and challenged the Muslims to a contest. The Prophet ﷺ asked Thabit ibn Qays to answer their speaker, and Hassan ibn Thabit their poet. After listening to both, Tamim’s chief al-Aqra’ said: "By my father, their speaker is more eloquent than ours, and their poet more poetic." They accepted Islam. The Prophet ﷺ honoured them with gifts.

When he sent Mu’adh ibn Jabal to Yemen, he told him: "You will come to a people from the People of the Book. Let the first thing you invite them to be the worship of Allah. When they know Allah, tell them that Allah has made five prayers obligatory on them in the day and night. When they do so, tell them that Allah has obligated zakah on them, taken from their rich and given to their poor. When they obey, then avoid taking the best of their wealth, and fear the supplication of the oppressed, for there is no veil between it and Allah." (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim)

He also told Mu’adh and Abu Musa: "Make things easy and do not make them difficult; give glad tidings and do not make people averse; and cooperate and do not differ." (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim)

In Dhul-Qa’dah 9 AH the Prophet ﷺ sent Abu Bakr to lead the Hajj. Just after he left, the opening verses of Surah al-Tawbah (Bara’ah) were revealed, ending the treaties with the idolaters who broke them and giving the others until their treaties ended. The Prophet ﷺ sent ‘Ali to announce it at Mina on the day of sacrifice. They announced that no idolater would perform Hajj after that year, and no one would circle the Kaaba naked (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). The next year was the Prophet’s ﷺ Farewell Pilgrimage.

facts: Khadijah, Sawdah, ‘A’ishah, Hafsah, Zaynab bint Khuzaymah, Umm Salamah, Zaynab bint Jahsh, Juwayriyah, Umm Habibah, Safiyyah, Maymunah
Al-Qasim, Zaynab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum, Fatimah, ‘Abdullah (with Khadijah); Ibrahim (with Maryam al-Qibtiyyah)
"The Prophet is closer to the believers than themselves, and his wives are their mothers" (33:6)
Rooms of mud brick and palm branches beside the mosque

s.h: In the service of his family
t: ‘A’ishah was asked what the Prophet ﷺ did at home. She said: "He used to be in the service of his family, and when the time for prayer came, he would go out for prayer." (Sahih al-Bukhari). She also said: "He used to mend his sandals, sew his garment, and do what men do in their homes." (Musnad Ahmad, sound). He milked his sheep, patched his clothes and helped with household work.

He told the Muslims: "The best of you are the best to their families, and I am the best of you to my family." (Sunan al-Tirmidhi). He said: "The believers with the most complete faith are those with the best character, and the best of you are the best to their women." (Sunan al-Tirmidhi)

He raced ‘A’ishah and she beat him; later, when she had put on weight, he beat her and said, "This is for that." (Sunan Abi Dawud). On a feast day, when Abyssinians were playing with spears in the mosque, he stood so she could watch behind him, his cheek touching hers, until she was tired (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). He said to her: "I know when you are pleased with me and when you are angry with me. When you are pleased, you say, No, by the Lord of Muhammad; when you are angry, you say, No, by the Lord of Ibrahim." She said, "Yes, by Allah, I only avoid your name." (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim)

When Fatimah entered, he rose, kissed her and sat her in his place; when he entered, she rose and kissed him (Sunan Abi Dawud and al-Tirmidhi). He said: "Fatimah is a part of me; whoever angers her angers me." (Sahih al-Bukhari). He wept when Ruqayyah died, and said "Join our righteous predecessor ‘Uthman ibn Maz’un," and he comforted the women who cried. He carried his grandchildren in prayer, and his grandson Hasan climbing on his back during prostration made him prolong it, until the child got down (Sunan al-Nasa’i).

His son Ibrahim died as a baby. The Prophet ﷺ took him in his arms, his eyes flowing with tears, and said: "The eyes shed tears and the heart grieves, but we say only what pleases our Lord. O Ibrahim, we are grieved by your parting." (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). When the sun was eclipsed on the day of his death, people said it was for Ibrahim; the Prophet ﷺ said: "The sun and moon are two signs of Allah; they do not eclipse for the death or life of anyone." (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim), correcting a mistaken belief in his own moment of grief.

facts: Eleven or thirteen rak’ahs, long and slow
Never criticised food; if he liked it he ate, if not, he left it
On a mat of palm fibre that left marks on his side
"I never saw anyone smile more than the Messenger of Allah" (al-Tirmidhi)
Pray as you saw me praying

t: ‘A’ishah described how he prayed: "Do not ask how beautiful and long it was." He would stand until his feet cracked (swelled). She said to him: "Why do you do this when Allah has forgiven you your past and future sins?" He said: "Should I not be a grateful servant?" (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). Hudhayfah prayed with him once and said that in a single rak’ah, he recited al-Baqarah, then al-Nisa’, then Al ‘Imran, slowly, and when he passed a verse of praise, he praised; of request, he requested; of refuge, he sought refuge (Sahih Muslim).

Abu Hurayrah said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never criticised any food. If he liked it, he ate it, and if he disliked it, he left it." (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). ‘A’ishah said that sometimes a month passed in which no fire was lit in the Prophet’s ﷺ household; they lived on dates and water (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). ‘Umar entered and saw him lying on a straw mat whose marks were on his side, with only a pillow of palm fibre and a skin hanging on the wall. ‘Umar wept, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "Are you not content that for them is this world and for us is the Hereafter?" (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim)

Jarir ibn ‘Abdullah said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never veiled himself from me since I accepted Islam, and he never saw me without smiling." (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). He joked and said only the truth. He once said to Anas, "O you of the two ears." (Sunan Abi Dawud and al-Tirmidhi). A man asked him for a mount; he said, "I will give you a baby of a she-camel." The man said, "What will I do with it?" He said: "Is there any camel which is not the baby of a she-camel?" (Sunan Abi Dawud and al-Tirmidhi). The Companions once asked: "O Messenger of Allah, do you joke with us?" He said: "Yes, but I only say what is true." (Sunan al-Tirmidhi)

Anas said that if a person took his hand, he did not withdraw it until the person did; if someone spoke to him, he listened until they finished; a slave woman could take him by the hand and lead him where she wanted (Sahih al-Bukhari). He sat on the ground, ate on the ground and said: "I am only a servant. I eat as a servant eats, and sit as a servant sits." (Musnad Ahmad and Ibn Sa’d). When he came to a gathering, he sat wherever there was room.

facts: A man forgiven for giving a thirsty dog water (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim)
A woman entered the Fire for imprisoning a cat (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim)
A camel complained to him about being overworked (Sunan Abi Dawud)
Burning a colony is not allowed (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim)
"There is a reward in every living creature" (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim)

t: The Prophet ﷺ said: "While a man was walking along a road, he became extremely thirsty. He found a well, went down, drank, and came out. Suddenly he saw a dog panting and eating mud out of thirst. He said: This dog has reached the same thirst that I had. So he went down into the well, filled his shoe with water, held it in his mouth, climbed up and gave the dog a drink. Allah thanked him and forgave him." The Companions asked: "O Messenger of Allah, is there a reward for us in serving animals?" He said: "In every living creature, there is a reward." (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim)

He said: "A woman was punished because of a cat which she had tied up until it died; she did not feed it or give it water, or let it eat from the vermin of the earth." (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim).

‘Abdullah ibn Ja’far narrated that the Prophet ﷺ entered the garden of an Ansari man, and there was a camel; when it saw him it groaned and its eyes filled with tears. He went to it, wiped behind its ears and it was quiet. He said: "Who owns this camel?" A young Ansari said: "Me, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Do you not fear Allah regarding this animal that Allah has given you? It complained to me that you starve it and overwork it." (Sunan Abi Dawud, sound)

On a journey, a Companion took the chicks of a hummarah bird, and the mother bird came, beating her wings over the Prophet ﷺ. He said: "Who has upset this bird by taking her chicks? Return them to her." And when he saw an ant colony that had been burnt, he asked who had burnt it; and he said: "It is not appropriate that anyone punishes with fire except the Lord of the fire." (Sunan Abi Dawud, sound)

Planting is charity (Sahih Muslim). He said: "If the Hour is established while one of you has a sapling in his hand, if he can plant it before the Hour comes, let him plant it." (Musnad Ahmad, sound). He taught moderation in the use of water, even for wudu (Sunan Abi Dawud).

facts: Uncle, foster-brother and age-mate of the Prophet ﷺ
About the 6th year of prophethood (as reported in the Sira)
"Asad Allah" (lion of Allah) and "Sayyid al-Shuhada’" (master of the martyrs)

t: The Sira says that Abu Jahl met the Prophet ﷺ at Safa, insulted him and struck him, and the Prophet ﷺ did not answer. A servant of ‘Abdullah ibn Jud’an saw it. When Hamzah returned from hunting, still carrying his bow, she told him. He went to the Kaaba, found Abu Jahl among Quraysh and hit him on the head with the bow, saying: "Do you insult him when I am on his religion, saying what he says? Hit me back if you can." Banu Makhzum rose to help Abu Jahl, but he told them to leave Hamzah, "for I did insult his nephew badly." Hamzah then reflected, and accepted Islam sincerely; his strength gave the Muslims more confidence.

At Badr, he fought in the front, and wore an ostrich feather as a mark; he killed Shaybah ibn Rabi’ah in the duel. The Quraysh lost people who were dear to Wahshi’s master, and Jubayr ibn Mut‘im promised Wahshi freedom if he killed Hamzah in revenge for his uncle. At Uhud, Wahshi hid behind a rock and threw his spear. Wahshi himself narrated it: "Hamzah was like a grey camel, cutting through the people with his sword... I hid behind a rock and threw; the spear went through his lower abdomen and came out between his legs." (Sahih al-Bukhari)

Hind bint ‘Utbah mutilated his body, and the Prophet ﷺ, seeing it, was moved, saying: "I have never stood in a place that angered me more than this." He said that if it were not that Safiyyah (Hamzah’s sister) would be grieved, he would leave him for the beasts. He wept so much that the Companions heard his sobbing, and he buried him with ‘Abdullah ibn Jahsh in one grave (as reported in the Sira).

After the conquest of Makkah, Wahshi fled to Ta’if; when the Thaqif delegation went to Madinah, he was told that the Prophet ﷺ does not kill envoys. He came, and said the shahadah. The Prophet ﷺ asked him how he killed Hamzah, and when he told him, he said: "Can you not hide your face from me?" Wahshi said he used to leave when he saw him. Later, Wahshi killed Musaylimah the liar at Yamamah with the same spear, and he said: "I hope that this atones for killing Hamzah." (Sahih al-Bukhari)

facts: Sayf Allah al-Maslul (the drawn sword of Allah)

t: As a young man of Banu Makhzum, Khalid inherited the cavalry command of Quraysh. He led the charge around the flank of the archers at Uhud and had a role in the pursuit of Muslims. At Hudaybiyyah he was sent to stop the Muslims and saw them praying Zuhr, and said, "They were off guard; we could have attacked." He is reported to have said: "I saw that this man is protected." Then, in his own account, he reflected: "Where could I go? To the Negus? To Heraclius? To the Persians? And live among the Arabs as an inferior?"

He travelled to Madinah, together with ‘Amr ibn al-‘As and ‘Uthman ibn Talhah, and accepted Islam. The Prophet ﷺ welcomed him: "Praise be to Allah who guided you; I have seen in you intelligence which I hoped would lead you to what is good." Khalid asked the Prophet ﷺ to pray for forgiveness for all that he had done in opposing him. He said: "Islam wipes out what came before it." (as reported in the Sira)

At Mu’tah, after the three commanders fell, the Muslims chose Khalid and he saved the army (see the account of Mu’tah). The Prophet ﷺ said: "The banner was taken by a sword from among the swords of Allah." (Sahih al-Bukhari). Under Abu Bakr, he put down the apostate Musaylimah at Yamamah and led an army to Iraq, and then marched across the Syrian desert in a famous forced march to reach the front at Yarmuk. Under ‘Umar, he was removed from command, which he accepted without complaint, saying: "I fight for Allah, not for ‘Umar," and served as a soldier.

On his deathbed in Homs, he is reported to have said: "I have fought in so many battles, and there is no place on my body without a scar from a sword, a spear or an arrow, and here I am dying in my bed like a camel. May the eyes of the cowards not sleep." He left his horse and weapons as charity in the cause of Allah. It is reported that ‘Umar wept for him and said: "Women will never give birth to the like of Khalid."

facts: Ghifar, near the road between Makkah and Syria
Early, said to be the fourth or fifth to do so
Al-Rabadhah, 32 AH, alone with his family
"No one under the sky is more truthful than Abu Dharr" (al-Tirmidhi)

t: He told Ibn ‘Abbas his own story (Sahih Muslim): "We were from Ghifar. I heard that a man had appeared in Makkah claiming to be a prophet. I told my brother Unays: Go to this man and bring me news. He went, came back and said: I saw him enjoining good character, and saying words that are not poetry. I said: You have not satisfied me. So I took a water skin and a bag of provisions and went to Makkah. I did not know him and did not want to ask anyone. I drank Zamzam and stayed in the mosque."

‘Ali saw him and took him to his home as a guest, without asking anything. The next day too. On the third day, ‘Ali asked what brought him. When Abu Dharr asked him to promise secrecy, he told him. ‘Ali said: "It is true, he is the Messenger of Allah. When you wake, follow me; if I see anything that worries me, I will stop as if to relieve myself, and if I walk on, follow me." He followed ‘Ali, entered the Prophet’s ﷺ place, and said: "Peace be upon you, Messenger of Allah." The Prophet ﷺ responded and he accepted Islam.

The Prophet ﷺ said: "Go back to your people, tell them, until you hear that we have prevailed." Abu Dharr said: "By the One who has your soul, I will proclaim it among them." He went to the mosque and shouted: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." The Quraysh rose and beat him until he fell. Al-‘Abbas, the Prophet’s ﷺ uncle, reached him and said: "Woe to you! Do you not know that he is of Ghifar, and your trade route to Syria passes through them?" They left him. The next day he did the same, and was beaten again, and al-‘Abbas saved him (Sahih Muslim). Then he returned to his people and invited them, and his tribe and the neighbours of Aslam accepted Islam.

The Prophet ﷺ once advised him: "O Abu Dharr, I see you are weak, and I love for you what I love for myself. Do not take charge of even two people, and do not take care of an orphan’s property." (Sahih Muslim). He lived in the desert settlement of al-Rabadhah, and warned the wealthy about hoarding. In the time of ‘Uthman, he expressed his views strongly. He died there in 32 AH, with only his wife and a servant, and as the Prophet ﷺ had foretold, a group of believers travelling from Iraq, among them ‘Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, passed by and buried him (Musnad Ahmad).

facts: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Sakhr al-Dawsi, called Abu Hurayrah (father of the kitten)
7 AH, then stayed with the Prophet ﷺ about three years

t: He said: "You say that Abu Hurayrah narrates a lot from the Prophet ﷺ. Allah is the Appointed Time. The Muhajirun were busy with trade in the markets, and the Ansar with their fields, and Abu Hurayrah stayed with the Prophet ﷺ to fill his stomach and attended when others were absent, and remembered when they forgot." (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). He once fell down in the mosque from hunger and people thought he was mad. Abu Bakr and ‘Umar passed by and did not understand his hint when he asked about a verse. Then the Prophet ﷺ came, knew from his face, said "Abu Hirr," and took him home and found a bowl of milk. He told him to call the people of the Suffah, and then to hand it to each of them until all had drunk, and last of all, he drank and the Prophet ﷺ drank. (Sahih al-Bukhari)

He said to the Prophet ﷺ: "I hear many hadith from you and forget them." He said: "Spread your cloak." He spread it, the Prophet ﷺ made a gesture as if scooping and putting something in it, and said: "Gather it." He gathered it, and said: "I never forgot anything after that." (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim)

His mother was an idolater, and he invited her to Islam every day. One day she said something about the Prophet ﷺ that grieved him, and he went in tears: "O Messenger of Allah, I invite my mother to Islam, and she refuses, and today I invited her and she said what I dislike. Pray to Allah to guide the mother of Abu Hurayrah." The Prophet ﷺ said: "O Allah, guide Abu Hurayrah’s mother." He ran back, heard water running, and when he entered, she said the shahadah. He went back weeping with joy and asked the Prophet ﷺ to pray that Allah make him and his mother beloved to the believers. (Sahih Muslim)

facts: About 27 years before the Hijrah, so about ten years older than ‘A’ishah
Al-Zubayr ibn al-‘Awwam, one of the ten promised Paradise

t: She narrates (Sahih al-Bukhari): "I prepared the provisions for the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr when they intended to leave for Madinah. I found nothing to tie the bag with, nor the water skin. I said to Abu Bakr: By Allah, I find nothing to tie it with except my waist-belt. He said: Split it in two, and tie the water skin with one and the bag with the other. I did, and that is why I was called Dhat al-Nitaqayn." She also came to the cave with food each evening.

Her grandfather, Abu Quhafah, who was old and blind and not yet Muslim, came when they left and said: "I think he has caused you grief by taking his money with him." She said: "No, grandfather, he left us a lot of good." She put pebbles in the niche where her father used to keep his money and covered it with a cloth, and put his hand on it to reassure him. He said: "If he has left it to you, he has done well." She said: "By Allah, he left us nothing, but I wanted to calm the old man."

When Abu Jahl and some men came to her door asking where her father was, she said: "By Allah, I do not know where my father is." Abu Jahl slapped her on the cheek so hard that her earring flew off (Sira). She did not tell.

She said (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim): "When al-Zubayr married me, he had no wealth or land or slave, nothing but his horse. I used to feed his horse, take care of it, grind the date stones for it and fetch water. I carried date stones on my head from al-Zubayr’s land that the Prophet ﷺ had given him, about two miles away. One day, I was carrying them, and I met the Prophet ﷺ with some of the Ansar. He called me and made his camel kneel to take me behind him. I was shy to go with the men and remembered al-Zubayr and his jealousy. He understood and went on." When she told al-Zubayr, he said that carrying the stones was harder for him than her riding with the Prophet ﷺ. Later Abu Bakr sent her a servant to take care of the horse, and she said: "It was as if he freed me."

Her son ‘Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr held Makkah against the Umayyad governor al-Hajjaj in 73 AH. Before the last battle, he came to his mother, who was blind and very old, and told her that his men were deserting. She said: "You know yourself best. If you are on the truth and calling to the truth, go on until you die for it; do not let the children of Umayyah play with you. If you wanted this world, you are a poor servant." He fought and was killed. She was told to be patient; she said: "How would I not be patient after he gave his life for Allah?" She died soon afterwards, a few days later, at around a hundred years old, with no tooth lost and no thought failing.

facts: Makkah, before the revelation (about 5 years before, in some accounts)
About six months after the Prophet ﷺ, in Ramadan 11 AH

t: As a young girl, she saw the persecution first-hand. When the Prophet ﷺ was praying at the Kaaba and Quraysh leaders threw the entrails of a camel on his back, it was Fatimah who came running, removed it, and scolded them (Sahih al-Bukhari). She also looked after her mother in her final days and in the hardship of the boycott.

s.h: The grinding stone and the tasbih
t: ‘Ali narrates (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim): "Fatimah complained of the effect of the grinding stone on her hands. She heard that some captives had been brought to the Prophet ﷺ, so she went to ask for a servant but did not find him; she told ‘A’ishah. When the Prophet ﷺ came, ‘A’ishah told him. He came to us when we had gone to bed. We started to get up, but he said: Stay where you are. He sat between us until I felt the coolness of his feet on my stomach. He said: Shall I not tell you of something better than what you asked for? When you go to bed, say Allahu akbar thirty-four times, Subhan Allah thirty-three times and Alhamdulillah thirty-three times. That is better for you than a servant." ‘Ali said: "I have never left it since I heard it from the Prophet ﷺ." Someone asked, "Not even on the night of Siffin?" He said, "Not even on the night of Siffin."

The Prophet ﷺ said: "Fatimah is a part of me, so whoever angers her angers me." (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). When she entered, he would stand, take her hand, kiss her and seat her in his place. In his final illness, he whispered to her; she wept; then he whispered again and she laughed. ‘A’ishah asked why, and Fatimah said later: "He told me he would die in this illness, so I wept; then he told me that I would be the first of his family to join him, so I laughed." (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). She died about six months after him.

facts: Into the tribe of Kalb, in the Syrian desert
Among the first four or five
Of the army at Mu’tah, where he was killed (8 AH)
Umm Ayman; later Zaynab bint Jahsh (divorced)

t: Zayd, about eight, went with his mother to visit her family when raiders captured him and sold him at ‘Ukaz. Hakim ibn Hizam bought him for his aunt Khadijah, who gave him to her husband, Muhammad ﷺ, before the revelation. Zayd’s father Harithah wept and wrote poetry looking for him. Years later, some men of Kalb saw him at Hajj and told his family.

Harithah and his brother travelled to Makkah with a ransom. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Call him and let him choose. If he chooses you, I will not ask for anything; and if he chooses me, then by Allah I am not one to prefer anyone over him." Zayd came, and was asked if he knew these men. He said: "Yes, this is my father and this my uncle." The Prophet ﷺ said: "You know me, and have seen how I treated you. Choose me or them." Zayd said: "I do not choose anyone over you. You are to me like my father and uncle." They said: "Woe to you, Zayd! You prefer slavery over freedom and your father and uncle?" He said: "Yes, I have seen something in this man that means I would not prefer anyone to him ever." The Prophet ﷺ took him to the Kaaba and announced: "Be witnesses that Zayd is my son; he inherits from me and I from him." His father and uncle left satisfied. (Sira)

After Islam, the practice of adoption making the adopted child a legal son was ended: "Call them by [the names of] their fathers; it is more just in the sight of Allah." (33:5) Then he was called Zayd ibn Harithah again. His marriage to Zaynab bint Jahsh did not last, and Allah then had the Prophet ﷺ marry her to remove the stigma of marrying a former adopted son’s wife: "So when Zayd had no longer any need for her, We married her to you." (33:37), which names him. ‘A’ishah said: "If the Prophet ﷺ had left him alive, he would have appointed him as his successor in the army." (Musnad Ahmad)

He led nearly every expedition he was sent on, and died carrying the banner at Mu’tah. The Prophet ﷺ went to Zayd’s daughter, who wept. He wept too. Sa’d said: "What is this, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The longing of the beloved for his beloved." (as reported in the Sira)

facts: The expedition of Sif al-Bahr (the whale), conquest of Syria

t: Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah narrates (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim): the Prophet ﷺ sent them, three hundred riders, with Abu ‘Ubaydah as commander, to intercept a Quraysh caravan, and gave them a bag of dates. Abu ‘Ubaydah gave them one date each day; then it ran out. They were so hungry that they ate leaves until their lips were swollen. Then the sea cast up a creature like a mound, called al-‘Anbar. Abu ‘Ubaydah first said it was carrion, then said: "No, we are the messengers of the Messenger of Allah, and in the way of Allah, and in need; so eat." They stayed there a month, until they became fat. Abu ‘Ubaydah had them stand a rib of the creature, and the tallest man with the largest camel passed under it without touching. When they returned, the Prophet ﷺ said: "It is a provision Allah has brought out for you. Do you have any of its flesh to give us?" They sent some, and he ate it.

When the delegation from Najran asked the Prophet ﷺ to send them a trustworthy man, he said: "I will send you a truly trustworthy man," and the Companions raised their necks hoping. He said: "Get up, Abu ‘Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah." (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). At Saqifah, when ‘Umar offered his oath of allegiance, Abu ‘Ubaydah said he would not take a position above a man the Prophet ﷺ had put forward to lead the prayer. As commander in Syria he took the surrender of Damascus, and when Heraclius lost, he lived as simply as the ordinary soldier.

In 18 AH, the plague of ‘Amwas spread in Syria. ‘Umar wrote to Abu ‘Ubaydah asking him to come to him in Madinah, as he had need of him. Abu ‘Ubaydah, knowing the reason, wrote: "I know your need. I am among Muslim soldiers and I will not leave them." When ‘Umar read, he wept. Abu ‘Ubaydah died of the plague with many others, including Mu’adh ibn Jabal, who succeeded him, and Yazid ibn Abi Sufyan. His last speech to the soldiers: "Praise Allah that the plague is a mercy from your Lord and the death of the righteous before you." Abu ‘Ubaydah is buried in the Jordan Valley.

facts: Madinah, about 20 years before the Hijrah
Sent to Yemen as a teacher and judge, 10 AH
"O Mu’adh, by Allah I love you"
On the Day of Resurrection "he will be raised as a leader of scholars" (reported)

t: The Prophet ﷺ took Mu’adh by the hand and said: "O Mu’adh, by Allah, I love you. So I advise you, O Mu’adh: do not neglect saying at the end of every prayer: Allahumma a’inni ‘ala dhikrika wa shukrika wa husni ‘ibadatika (O Allah, help me to remember You, to thank You and to worship You well)." (Sunan Abi Dawud and al-Nasa’i, sound). This is among the most beloved duas for completing prayer.

The Prophet ﷺ walked beside Mu’adh’s mount as he left, giving him advice, and said: "Fear Allah wherever you are; follow a bad deed with a good deed, which will erase it; and treat people with good character." (Sunan al-Tirmidhi). He said: "Make things easy and do not make them hard." He told him to teach first the oneness of Allah, and he warned him against taking the best of their property in zakah and against the dua of the oppressed (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim).

A report in Sunan Abi Dawud and al-Tirmidhi tells that when asked by what he would judge, Mu’adh said: "By the Book of Allah." "And if you do not find it?" "By the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah." "And if you do not find it?" "I will strive to form my own opinion, and not fall short." The Prophet ﷺ patted his chest and said: "Praise be to Allah who has made the messenger of the Messenger of Allah agree with what pleases Him." The chain of this report is disputed among scholars, but its meaning is accepted.

Once, he led his people in prayer after praying with the Prophet ﷺ, and recited al-Baqarah. A man left the prayer and prayed alone. Mu’adh was told and called him a hypocrite. The man complained to the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "O Mu’adh, are you putting people to trial? Recite al-Shams, al-Duha, al-Layl, al-A’la." (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). It is an example of a great scholar being corrected gently about the needs of those praying behind him.

facts: Born near Mosul; taken captive by the Byzantines, then sold to Makkah
The story of the boy and the king in Sahih Muslim
‘Umar appointed him to lead the prayer after him

t: He had been taken as a boy and grew up speaking Arabic with a Roman accent, which is why he was called al-Rumi. He became rich as a trader. When he said he would emigrate, the people of Makkah told him: "You came to us poor and with nothing, and now you have your wealth. By Allah, you will not leave with it." He said: "If I give you my wealth, will you let me go?" They said: "Yes." He gave them everything. (as reported in the Sira)

When he arrived at Quba, the Prophet ﷺ saw him and said: "The trade has profited, Abu Yahya," twice, and it is reported that Allah revealed: "And among the people is he who sells himself, seeking the approval of Allah. And Allah is kind to [His] servants." (2:207) (al-Hakim and others; some scholars grade the chain as weak, others as sound by corroboration).

He was known for his generosity: he would feed people until ‘Umar once told him: "I have heard that you give too much food away." He said: "The Prophet ﷺ said: The best of you are those who feed food and return the greeting." (Musnad Ahmad). When ‘Umar was stabbed, he told the people to wait for six men to choose a successor, and told Suhayb to lead the prayers for the community for the three days it took.
Suhayb narrated the long hadith of the boy, the king, the sorcerer and the monk (Sahih Muslim), which had in it all that he, an ex-captive, had understood about steadfastness.

facts: Thumamah ibn Uthal al-Hanafi, chief of Yamamah
Tied to a pillar of the Prophet’s Mosque
He stopped grain going to Makkah until the Prophet ﷺ permitted it

t: Abu Hurayrah narrates: "The Prophet ﷺ sent horsemen toward Najd and they brought a man from Banu Hanifah called Thumamah ibn Uthal, the chief of Yamamah. They tied him to one of the pillars of the mosque. The Prophet ﷺ went to him and said: What do you have, O Thumamah? He said: I have good, O Muhammad. If you kill me, you will kill someone with blood owed; if you show favour, you will favour a thankful man; and if you want wealth, ask and you will be given what you want. The Prophet ﷺ left him. The next day he asked: What do you have, Thumamah? He said: As I told you, if you show favour you will favour a grateful man. He left him until the day after, and asked again. He said: What I told you. The Prophet ﷺ said: Release Thumamah."

"He went to a date grove near the mosque, washed, and came into the mosque. He said: I bear witness that there is no god except Allah and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. O Muhammad, by Allah, there was no face on earth more hateful to me than your face, and now your face is the most beloved of faces to me. By Allah, there was no religion more hateful to me than your religion, and now your religion is the most beloved of religions to me. And no city was more hateful to me than yours, and now yours is the most beloved of cities to me. Your cavalry took me while I was intending ‘umrah. What do you think? The Prophet ﷺ gave him good news and told him to perform ‘umrah." (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim)

When he reached Makkah, someone said: "Have you become a Sabian (left your religion)?" He said: "No, I have accepted Islam with Muhammad. And no, by Allah, not a grain of wheat will reach you from Yamamah unless the Prophet ﷺ permits it." Yamamah was Makkah’s grain supplier. Quraysh wrote to the Prophet ﷺ, begging him in the name of kinship to tell Thumamah to let the grain through, and he did. The man whom Quraysh had considered an enemy of Muhammad became a friend who was able to help them because the Prophet ﷺ was merciful.

facts: Safanah (or Sufanah), daughter of Hatim al-Ta’i, and her brother ‘Adi
9 AH, after a raid on Tayy
"Grant me a favour, and may Allah grant you one"
Accepted Islam and was among those who defended the faith after the Prophet ﷺ

t: As the Sira tells, the women and children of Tayy were brought to Madinah after ‘Ali led a raid on the tribe, and housed near the mosque. Hatim’s daughter said: "O Messenger of Allah, my father has died, and the one who would help me is absent. Be kind to me, and may Allah be kind to you. I am the daughter of the chief of his people, who used to free captives, feed people, spread peace and fulfil needs, and never turned away a person in need. I am the daughter of Hatim al-Ta’i." The Prophet ﷺ said: "O girl, this is the character of the believers. If your father had been a Muslim, I would have asked for mercy on him. Free her, for her father loved noble character, and Allah loves noble character." She was freed.

She waited until a caravan from her people was going to Syria, and with the Prophet’s ﷺ help, travelled with them. She found her brother ‘Adi and said: "You have wronged your family by fleeing and leaving your family behind. Go to him quickly. By Allah, I have seen from him what I do not think any other would do." ‘Adi came to Madinah. The Prophet ﷺ took him to his house, offered him a cushion and sat on the ground. ‘Adi said: "By Allah, this is not the manner of a king." The Prophet ﷺ addressed him as a leader, and spoke of how many people would come to Islam, and how a woman would travel from al-Hirah to Makkah fearing none but Allah. ‘Adi accepted Islam. Later, he said he had seen the first and second come true: "the lady from Hirah" and that the treasures of Persia were opened (Sahih al-Bukhari).

facts: The Prophet ﷺ, from the people before us
A boulder closed the mouth of the cave
Each asked Allah by a deed done for Him alone

t: The Prophet ﷺ said that three men from before you set out until the night caught them, and they entered a cave to sleep. A rock fell from the mountain and blocked the mouth of the cave. They said to one another: "Nothing will save you from this rock except that you call upon Allah by your righteous deeds."

It is a picture of a situation with no human way out: three men in the dark, a rock too heavy for them, and nobody who knows where they are. In such a moment, the Prophet ﷺ tells us, what they reached for was not their rank, their strength or their money, but the sincerest thing each of them had done.

The first said: "O Allah, I had two elderly parents, and I would not give milk to my family or my slaves before them. One day my search for pasture took me far away, and I did not return until they were asleep. I milked for them and found them asleep. I disliked to wake them, and I disliked to give the family milk before them, so I stayed holding the bowl, waiting for them to wake, until dawn broke, while my children were crying at my feet. They woke and drank their evening milk. O Allah, if I did that for Your face, relieve us from the situation we are in because of this rock." The rock moved slightly, but not enough to leave.

The point is the priority he gave his parents over his own children, and the patience of someone who preferred to wait all night rather than interrupt their sleep. The Qur’an places kindness to parents directly after the worship of Allah (17:23).

The second said: "O Allah, I had a cousin whom I loved more than anyone, and I sought her, but she refused unless I brought her a hundred dinars. I struggled until I gathered it, and when I sat between her legs she said: Fear Allah, and do not break the seal except by right. I stood up and left her, and I left the gold I had given. O Allah, if I did it for Your face, relieve us." The rock moved further, but they still could not come out.

It echoes the verse: "And as for he who feared the position of his Lord and prevented the soul from [unlawful] inclination, then indeed, Paradise will be [his] refuge" (79:40–41). The strongest moment of desire became the strongest moment of fear of Allah.

s.h: The third man: trust with other people’s money
t: The third said: "O Allah, I hired workers and paid them all their wages except one man, who left without taking his. I invested his wage until it grew into a great deal of wealth. After some time he came and said: Servant of Allah, give me my wage. I said: All the camels, cows, sheep and slaves you see are your wage. He said: Do not mock me. I said: I am not mocking you. So he took it all and drove it away and left nothing. O Allah, if I did that for Your face, relieve us from what we are in." The rock opened and they walked out.

In this account the man had not stolen anything: he had simply handled someone’s money so well that it grew, and he could have kept the profit. The Prophet ﷺ tells it as a deed that opened the way for them.

s.h: What the story teaches about dua
t: The scholars take from this hadith that it is allowed, and good, to ask Allah by mentioning one’s own righteous deeds, in the way these men did, and that the deeds which count are those done purely for Allah, especially in private, where nobody sees them but Him.
It also fits the Qur’an’s promises: "I am near; I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me" (2:186), and "Whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out" (65:2).

facts: The Prophet ﷺ, about a man among the people before
Forgiven; the angels of mercy took him

t: The man had killed ninety-nine people. He asked about the most knowledgeable person on earth, and was directed to a monk. He came to him and said that he had killed ninety-nine, and asked: "Is there repentance for me?" The monk said: "No." So the man killed him and completed one hundred.

The hadith does not hide how far the man had fallen. It also shows how a well-meaning but incomplete answer, which closes the door of repentance, can push a wounded person to do even worse. That is why the Prophet ﷺ taught that people should be given glad tidings and not driven away.

He asked again about the most knowledgeable person on earth and was directed to a scholar. He said that he had killed one hundred, and asked: "Is there repentance for me?" The scholar said: "Yes. Who can stand between you and repentance? Go to such-and-such land, where people worship Allah, and worship Allah with them, and do not return to your own land, for it is a land of evil."

The scholar gave two things: the door is open, and the way through it is to change your surroundings. A person returning to the same friends, the same place and the same habits is returning to the same trap. So repentance here includes a physical journey.

He set out toward that land, and when he was halfway, death came to him. The angels of mercy and the angels of punishment disputed about him. The angels of mercy said: "He came repenting, turning with his heart to Allah." The angels of punishment said: "He never did any good."

An angel in the form of a man came to them, and they made him a judge between them. He said: "Measure the distance between the two lands. To whichever he is nearer, he belongs to it." They measured, and found him nearer to the land he was heading for, so the angels of mercy took him. In another narration, Allah commanded the land of the wicked to move away and the land of the righteous to come closer, and the distance was measured.

The story matches the verse: "Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful." (39:53) And the description of the servants of the Most Merciful in Surah al-Furqan includes those who killed and committed other major sins, then repented, believed and did righteous deeds: "For those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good" (25:70).

Scholars add that repentance for a killing also requires dealing with the rights of the victims’ families as far as possible, so the story is about the door to forgiveness being open, not about ignoring the rights of others.

facts: A man with leprosy, a bald man, and a blind man
Healing and wealth, then a request from a poor traveller

t: Three men of Bani Isra’il suffered: one had leprosy, one was bald, and one was blind. Allah wished to test them and sent an angel. The angel came to the leper and asked: "What is dearest to you?" He said: "A good colour and good skin, and that the people stop finding me repulsive." The angel wiped his body, and his sickness went; he was given good colour and skin.

Then the angel asked him which wealth he loved most. He said camels (or cows), and he was given a pregnant she-camel with the words, "May Allah bless you in it." The bald man asked for good hair, which he was given, and for cows, and was given a pregnant cow. The blind man asked for his sight to be restored, which was done, and for sheep, which were given in pregnancy.
The animals gave birth, and each man ended up with a valley full of camels, cows or sheep. After some time, the angel came back to each in the form he had known him before.

He came to the leper dressed as a leper and said: "I am a poor man whose means have been cut off on my journey; nothing will carry me today except Allah and then you. By the One who gave you your good colour, good skin and wealth, I ask you for a camel to take me to my destination." The man said: "I have many obligations." The angel said: "It seems that I know you. Were you not a leper whom people found repulsive, and a poor man, and then Allah gave you?" He said: "I inherited this wealth from one great man to another." The angel said: "If you are lying, may Allah return you to what you were."

s.h: The bald man and the blind man
t: The angel came to the bald man in the form he had known him and said the same thing; he too gave the same answer and received the same reply.

He came to the blind man in the form of a blind poor traveller: "I am a poor man and a traveller whose means have been cut off. Nothing will carry me except Allah and then you. I ask you by the One who returned your sight to you for a sheep to carry me on my journey." The man said: "I was blind and Allah restored my sight. Take whatever you wish, and leave whatever you wish. By Allah, I will never make it hard for you to take anything for the sake of Allah." The angel said: "Keep your wealth. You were all tested. Allah is pleased with you, and displeased with your two companions."

The Prophet ﷺ told this story to teach gratitude and humility. The leper and the bald man did not just refuse a request. They denied their own past, and so they denied the favour. The blind man named the favour directly: "Allah restored my sight," and that sentence turned his wealth into a means of giving.

The Qur’an says: "If you are grateful, I will surely increase you" (14:7), and the Prophet ﷺ said that the one who does not thank people does not thank Allah. The story also shows that a test can come disguised as an ordinary beggar at the door.

facts: His mother’s call while praying, then a false accusation
A baby spoke and cleared him

t: The Prophet ﷺ said that no one spoke in the cradle except three: ‘Isa, the companion of Jurayj, and another baby. Jurayj was a man who worshipped, and he built a hermitage and stayed in it. His mother came to him while he was praying and called: "O Jurayj!" He said: "O Lord, my mother and my prayer." He remained in his prayer, and she left.

The next day she came again, and he said the same. The third day she came and called, and he gave the same answer. She said: "O Allah, do not let him die until he sees the faces of prostitutes." The narration notes that if she had cursed him to be put to a trial, he would have been put to it.

Some Bani Isra’il were talking about Jurayj and his worship. A prostitute said: "If you wish, I will put him to a trial." She presented herself to him, but he did not look at her. So she went to a shepherd who took shelter in his hermitage, and he committed adultery with her, and she became pregnant. When she gave birth, she said that the baby was Jurayj’s.

The people came to him, brought him down, destroyed his hermitage and beat him. He said: "What is the matter with you?" They said: "You committed adultery with this prostitute and she has given birth to your child." He said: "Where is the baby?" They brought him. He said: "Leave me until I pray." He prayed, and when he finished he came to the baby, poked his stomach, and said: "O baby, who is your father?" The baby said: "The shepherd, so-and-so."

The people kissed Jurayj and began to touch him for blessing, and said: "We will build your hermitage from gold." He said: "No, rebuild it from clay as it was." And he did. The point of the story is the response: he did not ask for anything more than what he had before.

Scholars draw several lessons. One, that his mother’s right came before a voluntary prayer, so he should have answered her call, even though his intention was to stay in worship. Two, that Allah vindicates the sincere. Three, that sincerity does not need a reward in this world.

facts: Allah alone, by the borrower’s word
A hollowed piece of wood thrown into the sea

t: A man of Bani Isra’il asked another for a thousand dinars. The lender said: "Bring me witnesses to witness it." The borrower said: "Allah is sufficient as a witness." The lender said: "Bring me a guarantor." The borrower said: "Allah is sufficient as a guarantor." The lender said: "You have spoken the truth," and handed him the money for a fixed time.

It was extraordinary to lend such a large sum with no one but Allah as witness and guarantor. The Qur’an (2:282) normally advises writing down debts and bringing witnesses; the point is that this man trusted a man’s fear of Allah, and the borrower was true to it.

The borrower set out across the sea to settle his need. When the time came to pay, he looked for a ship to take him back, to pay what he owed, but found none. So he took a piece of wood, bored a hole in it, and put in a thousand dinars and a letter addressed to the lender, then sealed the hole. He took it to the sea and said: "O Allah, You know that I borrowed a thousand dinars from so-and-so. He asked me for a guarantor and I said Allah is sufficient as a guarantor, and he accepted. He asked for a witness and I said Allah is sufficient as a witness, and he accepted. I tried my best to find a ship to send him his money but I could not find one. I entrust it to You." Then he threw the wood into the sea.
He did not simply give up. He acted on every means open to him, then entrusted the rest to Allah.

The lender went out to look for a ship coming with his money. He found the piece of wood containing his money and took it home for his family as firewood. When he sawed it open, he found the money and the letter.

Some time later the borrower arrived with a thousand dinars, saying: "By Allah, I have tried my best to find a ship to bring you your money, but I could not find one before the one I arrived on." The lender said: "Did you send me anything?" He said: "Did I not tell you I could not find a ship?" The lender said: "Allah has delivered on your behalf what you sent in the wood. So take your thousand dinars back and go in guidance."

Scholars note that this is a story about two people who each had taqwa. The lender was generous in his trust and the borrower was determined to repay in full. It is also a story of tawakkul in its true sense: striving, then trusting.
The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever takes people’s wealth wanting to repay, Allah will help him repay it; and whoever takes it wanting to destroy it, Allah will destroy him (Sahih al-Bukhari 2387).

facts: An immoral woman of Bani Isra’il
She gave water to a thirsty dog
A woman was punished over a cat she starved

t: The Prophet ﷺ said that a prostitute was forgiven. She passed by a dog that was circling around a well and panting; thirst was about to kill it. She took off her leather sock, tied it with her head covering, and drew water for it. She was forgiven because of that.

Everything about the scene is ordinary. There was no audience, no gain, and no gratitude to be expected from a dog. It was a moment of pure mercy, and the Prophet ﷺ says Allah took it as the deed that outweighed her past.

s.h: A reward in every living creature
t: The Companions asked: "O Messenger of Allah, is there a reward for us in serving animals?" He said: "In every living moist liver there is a reward" (Sahih al-Bukhari 2363). This was said in another narration where a man gave water to a thirsty dog, and Allah thanked him and forgave him.
The meaning is that feeding or watering any creature with a living body is rewarded. It sits alongside the Qur’an’s statement that all creatures are communities like us (6:38).

The Prophet ﷺ also said that a woman entered the Fire because of a cat: she had tied it up, and did not feed it, and did not let it eat from the vermin of the earth until it died (Sahih al-Bukhari 3318, Sahih Muslim 2242).

Together these two hadith set the standard: cruelty toward a creature in your care is a serious matter, and kindness toward one in need can bring forgiveness. Kindness to animals is part of the religion, not an optional extra.

facts: A lender who gave people respite
"Overlook it; perhaps Allah will overlook our faults"

t: A man used to lend money to the people. When he sent his workers to collect, he used to tell them: "If you find someone in difficulty, forgive him. Perhaps Allah will forgive us." So when he met Allah, Allah forgave him.

The narration carries a simple equation: the one who forgives will be forgiven. It is the same principle as in the Qur’an: "Let them pardon and overlook. Would you not like that Allah should forgive you?" (24:22)

The Qur’an says: "And if the debtor is in hardship, then [let there be] postponement until [a time of] ease. But if you give [from your right as] charity, then it is better for you, if you only knew." (2:280) The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever gives a debtor in difficulty extra time will have the reward of a charity for each day of it (Musnad Ahmad, Sunan Ibn Majah), and that whoever gives respite to a debtor in difficulty or waives the debt will be shaded by Allah on the Day of Resurrection (Sahih Muslim 3006).
It is not asking creditors to lose what is theirs. It is inviting them to treat their rights as a means of reward, and to see the debtor’s distress as a human problem and not just a financial one.

The hadith has an application for any business. A trader who is gentle in how he sells, buys and collects what is owed is promised mercy: "May Allah have mercy on a man who is easy-going when he sells, when he buys and when he asks for what is owed to him" (Sahih al-Bukhari 2076).
The merchant in the story did not abandon his business. He built mercy into it, and Allah rewarded it.

facts: A jar of gold in a plot of purchased land
Each insisted the other should keep it
Marry the boy and the girl; spend on them and give charity

t: A man bought a piece of land from another man, and the buyer found a jar full of gold in it. The buyer said to the seller: "Take your gold from me. I bought land from you, I did not buy gold." The seller said: "I sold you the land and whatever is in it."

The scene is rare: two men each pushing the treasure toward the other. Fear of Allah made each of them careful about a doubtful thing, which is a form of the Prophet’s advice to leave what makes you doubt for what does not (Sunan at-Tirmidhi 2518).

They took their case to a man for judgment. The judge asked: "Do you have children?" One said: "I have a boy." The other said: "I have a girl." The judge said: "Marry the boy to the girl, spend on them both from it, and give charity."
The judge did not rule between claims. He found a solution that gave the gold a righteous use and linked the two families.
The message of the hadith is the contrast with how the world usually treats found treasure. In a time of disputes over money, here were two people disputing for the opposite reason.

It also fits the Qur’an’s warning against those who cheat in measure, taking in full from others but short-changing them (83:1–3). Here the opposite was true: both insisted on giving more than they had to.

The Prophet ﷺ said, in a hadith recorded by at-Tirmidhi and graded hasan: “The truthful, trustworthy merchant will be with the prophets, the truthful and the martyrs.” In another hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, he said: “The buyer and the seller have the right to cancel the sale as long as they have not separated. If they are truthful and make things clear, their sale is blessed. If they conceal and lie, the blessing of their sale is removed.”

The two men in the story of the gold are the picture of this hadith in action. Each of them is trying to give the other what is his, and each finds that what he has is more than enough. The judge’s answer, to marry their children and give some of it in charity, turns what could have been a dispute into a source of benefit for everyone. It is a reminder that honesty in business is a form of worship, and that its blessing is real.

facts: A prophet from the earlier prophets (not named)
An ant bit him, and he burned the ants’ colony

t: One of the prophets was sitting beneath a tree when an ant bit him. He ordered his belongings to be taken out from under the tree, and then the ants’ home was burned. Allah revealed to him: "Because one ant bit you, you burned a nation from the nations that glorify Allah?"

The narration is brief and is deliberately silent about which prophet it was. Its point lies in the revelation: the harm done to him was real, but it was one ant, and the response was far greater than the harm.

The Qur’an says: "The seven heavens and the earth and whatever is in them exalt Him. And there is not a thing except that it exalts [Allah] by His praise, but you do not understand their [way of] exalting." (17:44)

In Surah an-Naml, Sulayman hears an ant warn its fellows to enter their homes lest Sulayman and his army crush them unknowingly, and he smiles and asks Allah to make him grateful (27:18–19). It is the same Qur’anic picture of ants as a people with their own way.

The hadith does not forbid killing a harmful creature. Elsewhere the Prophet ﷺ allowed killing creatures that harm. What it teaches is proportion and restraint: that when we are hurt we should not escalate beyond what is needed.
It also shows the respect for the creatures of Allah in the Prophet’s teaching: even ants are a nation that praises Him.

s.h: Fire is for the Lord of fire
t: Another report ties the story to what the Prophet ﷺ taught about the ants and other creatures. ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud says in Sunan Abi Dawud: “We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey when he went off to relieve himself. We saw a small bird with two chicks, and we took the chicks. The mother bird came and began to beat the ground with her wings. The Prophet ﷺ came back and said: ‘Who has distressed this bird by taking her young? Return them to her.’ He also saw a village of ants that we had burned. He said: ‘Who burned this?’ We said: ‘We did.’ He said: ‘It is not fitting for anyone to punish with fire except the Lord of the fire.’”

The rule is known in the books of law: it is not permitted to burn a living creature, even a harmful one, when there is another way of killing it. Like the story of the prophet and the ant, it asks for proportion and compassion.

A third report fits with the first two. ‘Abdullah ibn Ja‘far says in Abu Dawud that the Prophet ﷺ entered the garden of a man of the Ansar, and there was a camel in it. When the camel saw the Prophet ﷺ, it moaned and its eyes ran with tears. The Prophet ﷺ went to it and stroked the back of its ears, and it grew quiet. He asked: “Who is the owner of this camel?” A young man of the Ansar said: “It is mine, O Messenger of Allah.” He said: “Do you not fear Allah regarding this animal which Allah has given you? It has complained to me that you keep it hungry and tire it out.”

It is one of the clearest hadiths on the rights of animals, and one of the best known. The Prophet ﷺ taught that an animal is a trust, that it feels, and that its owner will be asked about how he treated it.

facts: Asiya bint Muzahim (as named in the reports)
Among the women who reached perfection
"My Lord, build for me near You a house in Paradise"

t: The Qur’an tells that the mother of Musa, fearing for her baby, was inspired to place him in a chest and cast him into the river. "Then the family of Pharaoh picked him up that he would become to them an enemy and a [cause of] grief. Indeed, Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers were reasoners." (28:8)

It was the household’s decision to take the baby, but it was the wife of Pharaoh who spoke: "A comfort of the eye for me and for you. Do not kill him; perhaps he may benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son." And they did not perceive (28:9). The one who would one day challenge Pharaoh was brought up in his own home, because a woman in that palace had a merciful heart.
The Qur’an does not give a narrative of how Asiya came to believe. It gives only the result: she believed in the Lord of the worlds, in the palace of a man who said "I am your lord, the most high."

In Surah at-Tahrim, Allah offers two examples for the believers: the wife of Nuh and the wife of Lut, who were married to prophets and did not believe; and the wife of Pharaoh, who was married to a tyrant and did. It tells believers that what counts is each person’s own faith, and that no environment, however bad, makes a sincere person unable to hold on to it.

"My Lord, build for me near You a house in Paradise and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds and save me from the wrongdoing people." (66:11) Scholars have noted the order of the dua: "near You" before "a house", and the neighbour before the house. She asked first for being near Allah, then for the house.

She asked to be saved from Pharaoh and from his deeds, which means from the man and from what he did. The Qur’an does not say how she died. Some later reports describe torture, but they are not from sound sources, so IQRA leaves them out.

s.h: In the words of the Prophet ﷺ
t: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Many men have reached perfection, but no women have reached perfection except Maryam bint ‘Imran and Asiya the wife of Pharaoh, and the superiority of ‘A’ishah over other women is like the superiority of tharid (a dish of bread and meat) over other foods" (Sahih al-Bukhari 3411, Sahih Muslim 2431).
Asiya’s story belongs to everyone who has to practise their faith where it is not welcome: the dua she made is available to them.

facts: To place him in the river
He will be returned and made a messenger
Followed the chest and found where he went

t: "And We inspired to the mother of Musa, Suckle him; but when you fear for him, cast him into the river and do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and will make him [one] of the messengers." (28:7)

The word used is wahy, inspiration, which the Qur’an uses for what Allah puts into the heart of a person in a way that she recognises as true. Whatever form it took, she did not doubt it. She placed her baby in a chest and put it in the Nile, a thing no mother would do without being sure of the One who commanded it.

"And the heart of the mother of Musa became empty [of everything except the thought of Musa]. She was about to disclose [the matter concerning] him had We not bound fast her heart that she be of the believers." (28:10)

The Qur’an describes her state without softening it: she was a mother whose son was gone, and she nearly lost control. Allah’s support came in the form of a calm heart: "We bound her heart". So faith did not remove her sorrow, but it gave her the strength to carry it.

She told his sister to follow him. The sister watched him from a distance, and the household of Pharaoh did not notice. Musa refused all the wet nurses, and the sister said: "Shall I direct you to a household who will be responsible for him for you while they are to him sincere?" (28:12)

"So We restored him to his mother that her eye might be comforted and not grieve and that she would know that the promise of Allah is true. But most of them do not know." (28:13) She nursed him in safety, in Pharaoh’s own city.

The Qur’an mentions her again in Ta-Ha, in the list of Allah’s favours to Musa: "When We inspired to your mother what was inspired, [saying], Cast him into the chest and cast it into the river, and the river will throw it onto the bank, and there will take him an enemy to Me and an enemy to him." (20:38–39)
The Qur’an gives her no name, no tribe, no list of achievements. What it records is a mother who believed a promise from Allah and acted on it when she had every reason not to.

facts: To dedicate what is in her womb to Allah

t: "[Mention] when the wife of ‘Imran said, My Lord, indeed I have pledged to You what is in my womb, consecrated [for Your service], so accept this from me. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing." (3:35)

She did not know whether it would be a boy or a girl. She promised the child to Allah’s service, which at that time meant to be devoted to the house of worship. It was a hope that her child would be a servant.

"But when she delivered her, she said, My Lord, I have delivered a female. And Allah was more knowing of what she delivered, and the male is not like the female. And I have named her Maryam, and I seek refuge for her in You and for her descendants from Satan, the expelled [from the mercy of Allah]." (3:36)

Her disappointment was natural: according to the commentators, only males served in the temple. Yet the Qur’an says that Allah knew better what she had given birth to. She would be the mother of ‘Isa, and one of the women the Prophet ﷺ called perfect.

"So her Lord accepted her with good acceptance and caused her to grow in a good manner and put her in the care of Zakariyya." (3:37) Whenever Zakariyya entered the sanctuary, he found provision with her. He said: "O Maryam, from where is this to you?" She said: "It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without account."

Her mother’s dua of protection was answered. The Prophet ﷺ said: "There is no child of Adam but that Satan touches him when he is born, and he cries out because of the touch of Satan, except Maryam and her son" (Sahih al-Bukhari 3431).

facts: In the year 4 AH, as reported
Her judgement, and her narration of hadith

t: Umm Salamah and Abu Salama were among the early Muslims who migrated to Abyssinia. When they made the migration to Madinah, her family prevented her from leaving with her husband and kept her son from her. She sat each day in the valley and wept for about a year, until a relative took pity and let her go. She travelled the long road to Madinah with her son (as reported in the Sira, in Ibn Ishaq’s account).
She was one of those who endured the early Muslims’ trials in two lands, and she carried memory of it for the rest of her life.

When Abu Salama died, she said what the Prophet ﷺ had taught: "Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji’un. O Allah, reward me in my affliction and give me better in exchange." She said: "Who is better than Abu Salama?" Then Allah gave her the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (Sahih Muslim 918). The Prophet ﷺ said that no one is struck by a calamity and says this except that Allah replaces it with something better.

The Qur’an says: "And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits, but give good tidings to the patient, who, when disaster strikes them, say, Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return." (2:155–156)

After the treaty of Hudaybiyyah, the Prophet ﷺ said to his Companions: "Get up and sacrifice, then shave your heads." He said it three times, and nobody got up, for the terms had hit them hard. The Prophet ﷺ went in to Umm Salamah and told her. She said: "O Prophet of Allah, do you want this? Go out, and do not speak to anyone until you have slaughtered your sacrificial animal and called your barber to shave your head."

He did so, and when the Companions saw it, they got up, slaughtered, and began to shave each other’s heads, so that they almost killed each other in their grief (Sahih al-Bukhari 2731–2732). Her advice resolved a moment that commands had not.

Umm Salamah narrated many hadith and women would come to ask her what the Prophet ﷺ had said. She lived long after him and is counted among the last of his wives to pass away, in the years around 60 AH.
It is said that the Companions, men and women, consulted the wives of the Prophet ﷺ after his passing, for knowledge of his private life that they alone could give.

facts: Nusaybah bint Ka’b of the Banu Najjar, Umm ‘Umarah
One of two women who pledged allegiance
Fought to defend the Prophet ﷺ
Took part in the campaign against Musaylimah
Mostly the Sira, so details vary

t: Nusaybah was from Madinah. She and her husband attended the second pledge at al-‘Aqabah in the year before the Hijrah, where seventy-three men and two women pledged to protect the Prophet ﷺ as they protect their own families (reported in the Sira).
That pledge was the basis of the Hijrah. She was one of the women who took an active part in it.

When the Muslims were scattered at Uhud, the Prophet ﷺ was with a small group of Companions. As reported in the Sira, Nusaybah, who had been carrying water to the injured, took up the fight with a sword and a bow, shielding him. She received a deep wound in her shoulder, and counted a dozen wounds in all.

The Prophet ﷺ is reported to have said of her: "Whenever I looked to my right or left that day, I saw her fighting in front of me." He also prayed for her and her family that they be his companions in Paradise.

In the caliphate of Abu Bakr she asked leave to go out with the army against Musaylimah, who had claimed prophethood. She took part in the battle at Yamamah, where she lost a hand and was wounded again (as reported in the Sira). Her son Habib ibn Zayd had earlier been killed by Musaylimah, according to the same reports.
She lived on afterward. The Muslims remembered her for her courage in a time of danger and for her commitment to the Prophet ﷺ.

Most of what we know of Nusaybah’s fighting comes from the early biographies, such as Ibn Ishaq’s and Ibn Sa’d’s, rather than from the two Sahih collections. For that reason the details are given here as "reported", and the story should be read as a part of the Sira rather than as hadith.

The Qur’an says: "The believing men and believing women are allies of one another. They enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and establish prayer and give zakah and obey Allah and His Messenger." (9:71)

facts: Given to her by her mother Khadijah
Sunan Abi Dawud, and the Sira

t: Zaynab was the eldest of the Prophet’s daughters. She was married before the revelation to Abu al-‘As, a respected trader and a nephew of Khadijah. When the Prophet ﷺ began to call people to Islam, Zaynab believed. Her husband did not, though he did not turn against her or her faith. Quraysh pressed him to divorce her, but he refused.
The Hijrah came and Zaynab remained in Makkah with her husband, while her father and her sisters left (as told in the Sira).

At Badr, Abu al-‘As fought on the side of Quraysh and was taken captive. When Quraysh sent ransom for their prisoners, Zaynab sent money to free her husband, and with it a necklace that Khadijah had given her on her wedding day.

‘A’ishah reported that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw it, he was deeply moved for her sake, and said: "If you see fit to release her prisoner and return what she sent, then do so." The Companions said: "Yes", and they did so (Sunan Abi Dawud 2692). The sight of an object of Khadijah’s brought her back to his heart, and he asked for generosity, not as an order, but as a request they could refuse.

The Prophet ﷺ took a promise from Abu al-‘As that he would let Zaynab go to Madinah. He kept it. She set out, and some people from Quraysh tried to prevent her. During the encounter she was hurt and suffered a miscarriage, according to the biographies. She reached Madinah and lived in her father’s city.
It was some years before she was reunited with her husband.

Abu al-‘As later set out on a trading journey to Syria, and on his return a Muslim patrol seized his caravan. He slipped away at night to Madinah and went to Zaynab, who gave him protection. The Prophet ﷺ supported her protection, and the property was returned to him. He took it back to Makkah, gave everyone what they were owed, and then declared his Islam, and returned to Madinah (as reported in the Sira).
Zaynab died in 8 AH. The Prophet ﷺ taught the women who washed her, and is reported to have said of her that she was the best of his daughters, who suffered for his sake.

facts: Zihar: a pre-Islamic form of divorce
"Blessed is He whose hearing encompasses all sounds"

t: Khawlah came to the Prophet ﷺ and said that her husband Aws had said to her: "You are to me like the back of my mother." In the pre-Islamic custom of zihar, this was a divorce that was final but also left a woman in limbo, neither wife nor free. She told the Prophet ﷺ of her situation, her youth spent in his service, her old age, and her children.
The Prophet ﷺ said to her at first: "I do not see but that you are forbidden to him." She raised her hands and complained to Allah.

‘A’ishah said: "Blessed is He whose hearing encompasses all things. I was in the corner of the room and I could not hear some of what she said, and Allah revealed: Certainly has Allah heard the speech of the one who argues with you concerning her husband" (as reported by Ibn Majah, with a sound chain).

The Qur’an said that such a statement does not make a wife into a mother: "They are not their mothers. Their mothers are none but those who gave birth to them." (58:2) It called the practice "an objectionable statement and a falsehood" and gave an expiation.

The man who has done this must free a slave; if he cannot, fast two consecutive months; if he cannot, feed sixty poor people (58:3–4). Only then may he return to his wife. The Prophet ﷺ taught the man the rule, and the family continued.

A woman who had no power in the custom of her time was given a legal path in the revelation of her Lord. The Qur’an also records that Allah heard "the dialogue of you both" (58:1), a mark of care for the believers’ personal difficulties.

Her story was later told as an example of boldness in asking for justice. Some reports say that in the caliphate of ‘Umar she stopped him in the street and he listened to her with respect; these reports have weak chains, so they are noted here only as part of how the community remembered her.
The surah that carries her story was named for the way she argued: Al-Mujadilah, the woman who argues, or the woman who pleads her case.

facts: Nursemaid and carer of the Prophet ﷺ from infancy
Ubayd ibn Zayd, then Zayd ibn Harithah
Usamah ibn Zayd, whom the Prophet ﷺ loved

t: Barakah was an Abyssinian girl in the household of ‘Abdullah, the Prophet’s father. When ‘Abdullah died, she took care of his infant son, and when his mother Aminah died on the way back from Madinah, it was she who brought him to his grandfather, ‘Abd al-Muttalib (as told in the Sira).
The Prophet ﷺ is reported to have said: "Umm Ayman is my mother after my mother." He freed her when he inherited her, and he honoured her for the rest of her life.

She migrated to Madinah. She was at the battles of Uhud and Khaybar, as reported, where she gave water and treated the injured. The Prophet ﷺ arranged her marriage to his adopted son Zayd ibn Harithah, and their son was Usamah, whom the Prophet ﷺ loved so much that he was called "the beloved, the son of the beloved."
The Prophet ﷺ said of her: "Whoever wishes to marry a woman of Paradise, let him marry Umm Ayman" (reported by Ibn Sa’d; the chain is weak, so it is given here as part of how she was remembered).

Anas reported that after the death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abu Bakr said to ‘Umar: "Let us go to Umm Ayman and visit her, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to visit her." When they reached her, she wept. They said: "What makes you weep? What is with Allah is better for His Messenger." She said: "I do not weep because I do not know that what is with Allah is better for His Messenger. I weep because the revelation from heaven has ceased." This moved them, and they began weeping with her (Sahih Muslim 2454).
She understood the greatest loss: revelation, the direct guidance of Allah to His people, came to an end with the Prophet ﷺ.

facts: Khunays ibn Hudhafah, who died of wounds
The pages (suhuf) of the Qur’an after ‘Umar

s.h: A widow, then a wife of the Prophet
